re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ### What changed
Cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: a head-targeted dispatch for a fork PR reroutes onto the base repo's standard machine ref (`main`) with the PR number and a `refs/pull/<N>/head` checkout plan in the run inputs, instead of dispatching on the fork branch which 422s forever in the base repo (live fa pr-1591). # gh-1075: [GOAL] Fork PR dispatch: trigger on base ref + checkout refs/pull/N/head — cross-repo PRs are permanently undispatchable today (live: fa #1591 re-parked after rescue)

## Description

## Goal — cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: trigger on a base ref, check out refs/pull/N/head (v1)

One sentence: **a fork PR's legs run like any other PR's legs** — the SM dispatches the workflow on a base-repo ref with the PR number as input and the leg checks out `refs/pull/<N>/head` — instead of dispatching with `ref: <fork-branch>` which 422s forever.

Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — after the dead-head park fix (#1057, merged) and the fork-aware silent-update (#1070, merged), the THIRD fork-blind lane surfaced: the dispatch itself. Tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z: `pr-1591 dispatch dead-head (5/3 no-ref failures on fix/android-dap-home-sandbox) — validation_failed park`. The branch lives in the fork; `workflow_dispatch` with `ref: fix/android-dap-home-sandbox` in the base repo can never resolve → 422 "No ref found" → the gh-922 no-ref bookkeeping parks the PR — and because the park post-dates the last human push, the head-change reset never clears it. A fork PR is permanently undispatchable; every guest contribution dead-ends here.

## Root cause

`recordDispatchFailure` (js/smAgent.js:755+) treats a 422 on `ref: <branch>` as head-dead evidence — correct for same-repo PRs, structurally wrong for cross-repo PRs where the branch NEVER exists in the base repo. The dispatch contract itself (`ref: <head branch>`) assumes the branch is base-local.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Dispatch for a cross-repo PR triggers the workflow on the base default branch (or the repo's standard machine ref) with the PR number carried in inputs; the leg's checkout step resolves `refs/pull/<N>/head` (always fetchable, even when the fork branch is deleted). Same-repo PRs keep today's `ref: <branch>` dispatch (regression guard).
- **AC2** — A 422 no-ref failure on a cross-repo PR is never classified as head-dead (the head's liveness oracle for forks is `refs/pull/<N>/head`, per #1057) — no trigger-failure markers, no park accumulation.
- **AC3** — Genuinely dead fork heads (PR head ref unfetchable — fork deleted entirely) still park via the existing no-ref path, keyed to the pull-ref probe instead of the branch name.
- **AC4** — The leg's push-back path for fork PRs follows #1070's maintainer-edit contract (probe → push to fork / guest-park fallback) — no new push logic invented here.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — dispatch ref selection: fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PR → head branch (pure function, stubbed PR payloads).
- `UT-2` — no-ref classification: 422 on a fork branch name → NOT head-dead; unfetchable pull ref → head-dead (AC2/AC3).
- `IT-1` — simulated tick with a fork PR candidate: dispatch fires once, no park labels, checkout plan in the run inputs (AC1).
- `REG-1` — gh-922 bookkeeping tests (same-repo no-ref park after cap) stay green unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Running legs FROM the fork's workflow copy (untrusted code path — legs always run the base repo's workflow, checking out only the PR's data).
- Auto-merging fork PRs with failing validation (validation still required; this card only makes the legs runnable).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z ("dispatch dead-head 5/3 no-ref")
- js/smAgent.js recordDispatchFailure (:755+), js/sm/sources/githubSource.js no-ref classification (:141, :1136)
- Sibling fork-blindness cards: #1057 (park oracle — merged), #1070 (silent-update — merged), #1074 (failure observability)

## PR Description

Closes #1075
### What changed
Cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: a head-targeted dispatch for a fork PR reroutes onto the base repo's standard machine ref (`main`) with the PR number and a `refs/pull/<N>/head` checkout plan in the run inputs, instead of dispatching on the fork branch which 422s forever in the base repo (live fa pr-1591). The no-ref bookkeeping now keys fork heads to the `refs/pull/<N>/head` liveness probe instead of the branch name.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/forkDispatch.js`: `dispatchPlan` (fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PRs unchanged), `classifyForkNoRef`, `forkFullOf` (reuses the gh-1070 `validationLiveness.forkHeadFull` case-insensitive same-repo compare — no second resolver).

# gh-1075: [GOAL] Fork PR dispatch: trigger on base ref + checkout refs/pull/N/head — cross-repo PRs are permanently undispatchable today (live: fa #1591 re-parked after rescue)

## Description

## Goal — cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: trigger on a base ref, check out refs/pull/N/head (v1)

One sentence: **a fork PR's legs run like any other PR's legs** — the SM dispatches the workflow on a base-repo ref with the PR number as input and the leg checks out `refs/pull/<N>/head` — instead of dispatching with `ref: <fork-branch>` which 422s forever.

Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — after the dead-head park fix (#1057, merged) and the fork-aware silent-update (#1070, merged), the THIRD fork-blind lane surfaced: the dispatch itself. Tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z: `pr-1591 dispatch dead-head (5/3 no-ref failures on fix/android-dap-home-sandbox) — validation_failed park`. The branch lives in the fork; `workflow_dispatch` with `ref: fix/android-dap-home-sandbox` in the base repo can never resolve → 422 "No ref found" → the gh-922 no-ref bookkeeping parks the PR — and because the park post-dates the last human push, the head-change reset never clears it. A fork PR is permanently undispatchable; every guest contribution dead-ends here.

## Root cause

`recordDispatchFailure` (js/smAgent.js:755+) treats a 422 on `ref: <branch>` as head-dead evidence — correct for same-repo PRs, structurally wrong for cross-repo PRs where the branch NEVER exists in the base repo. The dispatch contract itself (`ref: <head branch>`) assumes the branch is base-local.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Dispatch for a cross-repo PR triggers the workflow on the base default branch (or the repo's standard machine ref) with the PR number carried in inputs; the leg's checkout step resolves `refs/pull/<N>/head` (always fetchable, even when the fork branch is deleted). Same-repo PRs keep today's `ref: <branch>` dispatch (regression guard).
- **AC2** — A 422 no-ref failure on a cross-repo PR is never classified as head-dead (the head's liveness oracle for forks is `refs/pull/<N>/head`, per #1057) — no trigger-failure markers, no park accumulation.
- **AC3** — Genuinely dead fork heads (PR head ref unfetchable — fork deleted entirely) still park via the existing no-ref path, keyed to the pull-ref probe instead of the branch name.
- **AC4** — The leg's push-back path for fork PRs follows #1070's maintainer-edit contract (probe → push to fork / guest-park fallback) — no new push logic invented here.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — dispatch ref selection: fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PR → head branch (pure function, stubbed PR payloads).
- `UT-2` — no-ref classification: 422 on a fork branch name → NOT head-dead; unfetchable pull ref → head-dead (AC2/AC3).
- `IT-1` — simulated tick with a fork PR candidate: dispatch fires once, no park labels, checkout plan in the run inputs (AC1).
- `REG-1` — gh-922 bookkeeping tests (same-repo no-ref park after cap) stay green unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Running legs FROM the fork's workflow copy (untrusted code path — legs always run the base repo's workflow, checking out only the PR's data).
- Auto-merging fork PRs with failing validation (validation still required; this card only makes the legs runnable).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z ("dispatch dead-head 5/3 no-ref")
- js/smAgent.js recordDispatchFailure (:755+), js/sm/sources/githubSource.js no-ref classification (:141, :1136)
- Sibling fork-blindness cards: #1057 (park oracle — merged), #1070 (silent-update — merged), #1074 (failure observability)

### What changed
Cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: a head-targeted dispatch for a fork PR reroutes onto the base repo's standard machine ref (`main`) with the PR number and a `refs/pull/<N>/head` checkout plan in the run inputs, instead of dispatching on the fork branch which 422s forever in the base repo (live fa pr-1591). # gh-1075: [GOAL] Fork PR dispatch: trigger on base ref + checkout refs/pull/N/head — cross-repo PRs are permanently undispatchable today (live: fa #1591 re-parked after rescue)

## Description

## Goal — cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: trigger on a base ref, check out refs/pull/N/head (v1)

One sentence: **a fork PR's legs run like any other PR's legs** — the SM dispatches the workflow on a base-repo ref with the PR number as input and the leg checks out `refs/pull/<N>/head` — instead of dispatching with `ref: <fork-branch>` which 422s forever.

Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — after the dead-head park fix (#1057, merged) and the fork-aware silent-update (#1070, merged), the THIRD fork-blind lane surfaced: the dispatch itself. Tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z: `pr-1591 dispatch dead-head (5/3 no-ref failures on fix/android-dap-home-sandbox) — validation_failed park`. The branch lives in the fork; `workflow_dispatch` with `ref: fix/android-dap-home-sandbox` in the base repo can never resolve → 422 "No ref found" → the gh-922 no-ref bookkeeping parks the PR — and because the park post-dates the last human push, the head-change reset never clears it. A fork PR is permanently undispatchable; every guest contribution dead-ends here.

## Root cause

`recordDispatchFailure` (js/smAgent.js:755+) treats a 422 on `ref: <branch>` as head-dead evidence — correct for same-repo PRs, structurally wrong for cross-repo PRs where the branch NEVER exists in the base repo. The dispatch contract itself (`ref: <head branch>`) assumes the branch is base-local.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Dispatch for a cross-repo PR triggers the workflow on the base default branch (or the repo's standard machine ref) with the PR number carried in inputs; the leg's checkout step resolves `refs/pull/<N>/head` (always fetchable, even when the fork branch is deleted). Same-repo PRs keep today's `ref: <branch>` dispatch (regression guard).
- **AC2** — A 422 no-ref failure on a cross-repo PR is never classified as head-dead (the head's liveness oracle for forks is `refs/pull/<N>/head`, per #1057) — no trigger-failure markers, no park accumulation.
- **AC3** — Genuinely dead fork heads (PR head ref unfetchable — fork deleted entirely) still park via the existing no-ref path, keyed to the pull-ref probe instead of the branch name.
- **AC4** — The leg's push-back path for fork PRs follows #1070's maintainer-edit contract (probe → push to fork / guest-park fallback) — no new push logic invented here.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — dispatch ref selection: fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PR → head branch (pure function, stubbed PR payloads).
- `UT-2` — no-ref classification: 422 on a fork branch name → NOT head-dead; unfetchable pull ref → head-dead (AC2/AC3).
- `IT-1` — simulated tick with a fork PR candidate: dispatch fires once, no park labels, checkout plan in the run inputs (AC1).
- `REG-1` — gh-922 bookkeeping tests (same-repo no-ref park after cap) stay green unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Running legs FROM the fork's workflow copy (untrusted code path — legs always run the base repo's workflow, checking out only the PR's data).
- Auto-merging fork PRs with failing validation (validation still required; this card only makes the legs runnable).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z ("dispatch dead-head 5/3 no-ref")
- js/smAgent.js recordDispatchFailure (:755+), js/sm/sources/githubSource.js no-ref classification (:141, :1136)
- Sibling fork-blindness cards: #1057 (park oracle — merged), #1070 (silent-update — merged), #1074 (failure observability)

# gh-1075: [GOAL] Fork PR dispatch: trigger on base ref + checkout refs/pull/N/head — cross-repo PRs are permanently undispatchable today (live: fa #1591 re-parked after rescue)

## Description

## Goal — cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: trigger on a base ref, check out refs/pull/N/head (v1)

One sentence: **a fork PR's legs run like any other PR's legs** — the SM dispatches the workflow on a base-repo ref with the PR number as input and the leg checks out `refs/pull/<N>/head` — instead of dispatching with `ref: <fork-branch>` which 422s forever.

Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — after the dead-head park fix (#1057, merged) and the fork-aware silent-update (#1070, merged), the THIRD fork-blind lane surfaced: the dispatch itself. Tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z: `pr-1591 dispatch dead-head (5/3 no-ref failures on fix/android-dap-home-sandbox) — validation_failed park`. The branch lives in the fork; `workflow_dispatch` with `ref: fix/android-dap-home-sandbox` in the base repo can never resolve → 422 "No ref found" → the gh-922 no-ref bookkeeping parks the PR — and because the park post-dates the last human push, the head-change reset never clears it. A fork PR is permanently undispatchable; every guest contribution dead-ends here.

## Root cause

`recordDispatchFailure` (js/smAgent.js:755+) treats a 422 on `ref: <branch>` as head-dead evidence — correct for same-repo PRs, structurally wrong for cross-repo PRs where the branch NEVER exists in the base repo. The dispatch contract itself (`ref: <head branch>`) assumes the branch is base-local.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Dispatch for a cross-repo PR triggers the workflow on the base default branch (or the repo's standard machine ref) with the PR number carried in inputs; the leg's checkout step resolves `refs/pull/<N>/head` (always fetchable, even when the fork branch is deleted). Same-repo PRs keep today's `ref: <branch>` dispatch (regression guard).
- **AC2** — A 422 no-ref failure on a cross-repo PR is never classified as head-dead (the head's liveness oracle for forks is `refs/pull/<N>/head`, per #1057) — no trigger-failure markers, no park accumulation.
- **AC3** — Genuinely dead fork heads (PR head ref unfetchable — fork deleted entirely) still park via the existing no-ref path, keyed to the pull-ref probe instead of the branch name.
- **AC4** — The leg's push-back path for fork PRs follows #1070's maintainer-edit contract (probe → push to fork / guest-park fallback) — no new push logic invented here.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — dispatch ref selection: fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PR → head branch (pure function, stubbed PR payloads).
- `UT-2` — no-ref classification: 422 on a fork branch name → NOT head-dead; unfetchable pull ref → head-dead (AC2/AC3).
- `IT-1` — simulated tick with a fork PR candidate: dispatch fires once, no park labels, checkout plan in the run inputs (AC1).
- `REG-1` — gh-922 bookkeeping tests (same-repo no-ref park after cap) stay green unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Running legs FROM the fork's workflow copy (untrusted code path — legs always run the base repo's workflow, checking out only the PR's data).
- Auto-merging fork PRs with failing validation (validation still required; this card only makes the legs runnable).

- js/smAgent.js recordDispatchFailure (:755+), js/sm/sources/githubSource.js no-ref classification (:141, :1136)

## PR Description

Closes #1075
### What changed
Cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: a head-targeted dispatch for a fork PR reroutes onto the base repo's standard machine ref (`main`) with the PR number and a `refs/pull/<N>/head` checkout plan in the run inputs, instead of dispatching on the fork branch which 422s forever in the base repo (live fa pr-1591). The no-ref bookkeeping now keys fork heads to the `refs/pull/<N>/head` liveness probe instead of the branch name.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/forkDispatch.js`: `dispatchPlan` (fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PRs unchanged), `classifyForkNoRef`, `forkFullOf` (reuses the gh-1070 `validationLiveness.forkHeadFull` case-insensitive same-repo compare — no second resolver).
- `triggerWorkflow` applies the plan before dispatch and backfills `inputs.pr` only when the rule carried no `{prNumber}`; the gh-1028 branch-leg guard keeps its pre-gh-1075 semantics via a captured `headRefDispatch` flag.
- `recordDispatchFailure`: a no-ref failure on a fork PR runs an `ls-remote refs/pull/<N>/head` probe (fail-open to LIVE) — fetchable → never head-dead, no markers/park (AC2); unfetchable → parks through the existing gh-922 path keyed on the pull ref (AC3). Same-repo bookkeeping is byte-identical (REG-1); the gh-1028/715/1029 guards and the leg push-back (#1070 contract) are untouched.
- Leg checkout/push consumption of the `checkout_ref` input is deliberately out of scope (card non-goals; #1074 owns failure observability).

dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_forkDispatch.json   # UT-1/UT-2 pure contract (12 tests)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json        # IT-1/AC2/AC3/REG-1 tick suites (623 tests)

## Description

## Goal — cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: trigger on a base ref, check out refs/pull/N/head (v1)

One sentence: **a fork PR's legs run like any other PR's legs** — the SM dispatches the workflow on a base-repo ref with the PR number as input and the leg checks out `refs/pull/<N>/head` — instead of dispatching with `ref: <fork-branch>` which 422s forever.

Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — after the dead-head park fix (#1057, merged) and the fork-aware silent-update (#1070, merged), the THIRD fork-blind lane surfaced: the dispatch itself. Tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z: `pr-1591 dispatch dead-head (5/3 no-ref failures on fix/android-dap-home-sandbox) — validation_failed park`. The branch lives in the fork; `workflow_dispatch` with `ref: fix/android-dap-home-sandbox` in the base repo can never resolve → 422 "No ref found" → the gh-922 no-ref bookkeeping parks the PR — and because the park post-dates the last human push, the head-change reset never clears it. A fork PR is permanently undispatchable; every guest contribution dead-ends here.

## Root cause

`recordDispatchFailure` (js/smAgent.js:755+) treats a 422 on `ref: <branch>` as head-dead evidence — correct for same-repo PRs, structurally wrong for cross-repo PRs where the branch NEVER exists in the base repo. The dispatch contract itself (`ref: <head branch>`) assumes the branch is base-local.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Dispatch for a cross-repo PR triggers the workflow on the base default branch (or the repo's standard machine ref) with the PR number carried in inputs; the leg's checkout step resolves `refs/pull/<N>/head` (always fetchable, even when the fork branch is deleted). Same-repo PRs keep today's `ref: <branch>` dispatch (regression guard).
- **AC2** — A 422 no-ref failure on a cross-repo PR is never classified as head-dead (the head's liveness oracle for forks is `refs/pull/<N>/head`, per #1057) — no trigger-failure markers, no park accumulation.
- **AC3** — Genuinely dead fork heads (PR head ref unfetchable — fork deleted entirely) still park via the existing no-ref path, keyed to the pull-ref probe instead of the branch name.
- **AC4** — The leg's push-back path for fork PRs follows #1070's maintainer-edit contract (probe → push to fork / guest-park fallback) — no new push logic invented here.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — dispatch ref selection: fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PR → head branch (pure function, stubbed PR payloads).
- `UT-2` — no-ref classification: 422 on a fork branch name → NOT head-dead; unfetchable pull ref → head-dead (AC2/AC3).
- `IT-1` — simulated tick with a fork PR candidate: dispatch fires once, no park labels, checkout plan in the run inputs (AC1).
- `REG-1` — gh-922 bookkeeping tests (same-repo no-ref park after cap) stay green unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Running legs FROM the fork's workflow copy (untrusted code path — legs always run the base repo's workflow, checking out only the PR's data).
- Auto-merging fork PRs with failing validation (validation still required; this card only makes the legs runnable).

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ### What changed
Cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: a head-targeted dispatch for a fork PR reroutes onto the base repo's standard machine ref (`main`) with the PR number and a `refs/pull/<N>/head` checkout plan in the run inputs, instead of dispatching on the fork branch which 422s forever in the base repo (live fa pr-1591). # gh-1075: [GOAL] Fork PR dispatch: trigger on base ref + checkout refs/pull/N/head — cross-repo PRs are permanently undispatchable today (live: fa #1591 re-parked after rescue)

## Description

## Goal — cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: trigger on a base ref, check out refs/pull/N/head (v1)

One sentence: **a fork PR's legs run like any other PR's legs** — the SM dispatches the workflow on a base-repo ref with the PR number as input and the leg checks out `refs/pull/<N>/head` — instead of dispatching with `ref: <fork-branch>` which 422s forever.

Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — after the dead-head park fix (#1057, merged) and the fork-aware silent-update (#1070, merged), the THIRD fork-blind lane surfaced: the dispatch itself. Tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z: `pr-1591 dispatch dead-head (5/3 no-ref failures on fix/android-dap-home-sandbox) — validation_failed park`. The branch lives in the fork; `workflow_dispatch` with `ref: fix/android-dap-home-sandbox` in the base repo can never resolve → 422 "No ref found" → the gh-922 no-ref bookkeeping parks the PR — and because the park post-dates the last human push, the head-change reset never clears it. A fork PR is permanently undispatchable; every guest contribution dead-ends here.

## Root cause

`recordDispatchFailure` (js/smAgent.js:755+) treats a 422 on `ref: <branch>` as head-dead evidence — correct for same-repo PRs, structurally wrong for cross-repo PRs where the branch NEVER exists in the base repo. The dispatch contract itself (`ref: <head branch>`) assumes the branch is base-local.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Dispatch for a cross-repo PR triggers the workflow on the base default branch (or the repo's standard machine ref) with the PR number carried in inputs; the leg's checkout step resolves `refs/pull/<N>/head` (always fetchable, even when the fork branch is deleted). Same-repo PRs keep today's `ref: <branch>` dispatch (regression guard).
- **AC2** — A 422 no-ref failure on a cross-repo PR is never classified as head-dead (the head's liveness oracle for forks is `refs/pull/<N>/head`, per #1057) — no trigger-failure markers, no park accumulation.
- **AC3** — Genuinely dead fork heads (PR head ref unfetchable — fork deleted entirely) still park via the existing no-ref path, keyed to the pull-ref probe instead of the branch name.
- **AC4** — The leg's push-back path for fork PRs follows #1070's maintainer-edit contract (probe → push to fork / guest-park fallback) — no new push logic invented here.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — dispatch ref selection: fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PR → head branch (pure function, stubbed PR payloads).
- `UT-2` — no-ref classification: 422 on a fork branch name → NOT head-dead; unfetchable pull ref → head-dead (AC2/AC3).
- `IT-1` — simulated tick with a fork PR candidate: dispatch fires once, no park labels, checkout plan in the run inputs (AC1).
- `REG-1` — gh-922 bookkeeping tests (same-repo no-ref park after cap) stay green unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Running legs FROM the fork's workflow copy (untrusted code path — legs always run the base repo's workflow, checking out only the PR's data).
- Auto-merging fork PRs with failing validation (validation still required; this card only makes the legs runnable).

## References

# gh-1075: [GOAL] Fork PR dispatch: trigger on base ref + checkout refs/pull/N/head — cross-repo PRs are permanently undispatchable today (live: fa #1591 re-parked after rescue)

## Description

## Goal — cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: trigger on a base ref, check out refs/pull/N/head (v1)

One sentence: **a fork PR's legs run like any other PR's legs** — the SM dispatches the workflow on a base-repo ref with the PR number as input and the leg checks out `refs/pull/<N>/head` — instead of dispatching with `ref: <fork-branch>` which 422s forever.

Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — after the dead-head park fix (#1057, merged) and the fork-aware silent-update (#1070, merged), the THIRD fork-blind lane surfaced: the dispatch itself. Tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z: `pr-1591 dispatch dead-head (5/3 no-ref failures on fix/android-dap-home-sandbox) — validation_failed park`. The branch lives in the fork; `workflow_dispatch` with `ref: fix/android-dap-home-sandbox` in the base repo can never resolve → 422 "No ref found" → the gh-922 no-ref bookkeeping parks the PR — and because the park post-dates the last human push, the head-change reset never clears it. A fork PR is permanently undispatchable; every guest contribution dead-ends here.

## Root cause

`recordDispatchFailure` (js/smAgent.js:755+) treats a 422 on `ref: <branch>` as head-dead evidence — correct for same-repo PRs, structurally wrong for cross-repo PRs where the branch NEVER exists in the base repo. The dispatch contract itself (`ref: <head branch>`) assumes the branch is base-local.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Dispatch for a cross-repo PR triggers the workflow on the base default branch (or the repo's standard machine ref) with the PR number carried in inputs; the leg's checkout step resolves `refs/pull/<N>/head` (always fetchable, even when the fork branch is deleted). Same-repo PRs keep today's `ref: <branch>` dispatch (regression guard).
- **AC2** — A 422 no-ref failure on a cross-repo PR is never classified as head-dead (the head's liveness oracle for forks is `refs/pull/<N>/head`, per #1057) — no trigger-failure markers, no park accumulation.
- **AC3** — Genuinely dead fork heads (PR head ref unfetchable — fork deleted entirely) still park via the existing no-ref path, keyed to the pull-ref probe instead of the branch name.
- **AC4** — The leg's push-back path for fork PRs follows #1070's maintainer-edit contract (probe → push to fork / guest-park fallback) — no new push logic invented here.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — dispatch ref selection: fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PR → head branch (pure function, stubbed PR payloads).
- `UT-2` — no-ref classification: 422 on a fork branch name → NOT head-dead; unfetchable pull ref → head-dead (AC2/AC3).
- `IT-1` — simulated tick with a fork PR candidate: dispatch fires once, no park labels, checkout plan in the run inputs (AC1).
- `REG-1` — gh-922 bookkeeping tests (same-repo no-ref park after cap) stay green unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Running legs FROM the fork's workflow copy (untrusted code path — legs always run the base repo's workflow, checking out only the PR's data).
- Auto-merging fork PRs with failing validation (validation still required; this card only makes the legs runnable).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z ("dispatch dead-head 5/3 no-ref")

- Sibling fork-blindness cards: #1057 (park oracle — merged), #1070 (silent-update — merged), #1074 (failure observability)

Cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: a head-targeted dispatch for a fork PR reroutes onto the base repo's standard machine ref (`main`) with the PR number and a `refs/pull/<N>/head` checkout plan in the run inputs, instead of dispatching on the fork branch which 422s forever in the base repo (live fa pr-1591). # gh-1075: [GOAL] Fork PR dispatch: trigger on base ref + checkout refs/pull/N/head — cross-repo PRs are permanently undispatchable today (live: fa #1591 re-parked after rescue)

## Description

## Goal — cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: trigger on a base ref, check out refs/pull/N/head (v1)

One sentence: **a fork PR's legs run like any other PR's legs** — the SM dispatches the workflow on a base-repo ref with the PR number as input and the leg checks out `refs/pull/<N>/head` — instead of dispatching with `ref: <fork-branch>` which 422s forever.

Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — after the dead-head park fix (#1057, merged) and the fork-aware silent-update (#1070, merged), the THIRD fork-blind lane surfaced: the dispatch itself. Tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z: `pr-1591 dispatch dead-head (5/3 no-ref failures on fix/android-dap-home-sandbox) — validation_failed park`. The branch lives in the fork; `workflow_dispatch` with `ref: fix/android-dap-home-sandbox` in the base repo can never resolve → 422 "No ref found" → the gh-922 no-ref bookkeeping parks the PR — and because the park post-dates the last human push, the head-change reset never clears it. A fork PR is permanently undispatchable; every guest contribution dead-ends here.

## Root cause

`recordDispatchFailure` (js/smAgent.js:755+) treats a 422 on `ref: <branch>` as head-dead evidence — correct for same-repo PRs, structurally wrong for cross-repo PRs where the branch NEVER exists in the base repo. The dispatch contract itself (`ref: <head branch>`) assumes the branch is base-local.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Dispatch for a cross-repo PR triggers the workflow on the base default branch (or the repo's standard machine ref) with the PR number carried in inputs; the leg's checkout step resolves `refs/pull/<N>/head` (always fetchable, even when the fork branch is deleted). Same-repo PRs keep today's `ref: <branch>` dispatch (regression guard).
- **AC2** — A 422 no-ref failure on a cross-repo PR is never classified as head-dead (the head's liveness oracle for forks is `refs/pull/<N>/head`, per #1057) — no trigger-failure markers, no park accumulation.
- **AC3** — Genuinely dead fork heads (PR head ref unfetchable — fork deleted entirely) still park via the existing no-ref path, keyed to the pull-ref probe instead of the branch name.
- **AC4** — The leg's push-back path for fork PRs follows #1070's maintainer-edit contract (probe → push to fork / guest-park fallback) — no new push logic invented here.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — dispatch ref selection: fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PR → head branch (pure function, stubbed PR payloads).
- `UT-2` — no-ref classification: 422 on a fork branch name → NOT head-dead; unfetchable pull ref → head-dead (AC2/AC3).
- `IT-1` — simulated tick with a fork PR candidate: dispatch fires once, no park labels, checkout plan in the run inputs (AC1).
- `REG-1` — gh-922 bookkeeping tests (same-repo no-ref park after cap) stay green unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Running legs FROM the fork's workflow copy (untrusted code path — legs always run the base repo's workflow, checking out only the PR's data).
- Auto-merging fork PRs with failing validation (validation still required; this card only makes the legs runnable).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z ("dispatch dead-head 5/3 no-ref")
- js/smAgent.js recordDispatchFailure (:755+), js/sm/sources/githubSource.js no-ref classification (:141, :1136)
- Sibling fork-blindness cards: #1057 (park oracle — merged), #1070 (silent-update — merged), #1074 (failure observability)

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ### What changed
Cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: a head-targeted dispatch for a fork PR reroutes onto the base repo's standard machine ref (`main`) with the PR number and a `refs/pull/<N>/head` checkout plan in the run inputs, instead of dispatching on the fork branch which 422s forever in the base repo (live fa pr-1591). # gh-1075: [GOAL] Fork PR dispatch: trigger on base ref + checkout refs/pull/N/head — cross-repo PRs are permanently undispatchable today (live: fa #1591 re-parked after rescue)

## Description

## Goal — cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: trigger on a base ref, check out refs/pull/N/head (v1)

One sentence: **a fork PR's legs run like any other PR's legs** — the SM dispatches the workflow on a base-repo ref with the PR number as input and the leg checks out `refs/pull/<N>/head` — instead of dispatching with `ref: <fork-branch>` which 422s forever.

Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — after the dead-head park fix (#1057, merged) and the fork-aware silent-update (#1070, merged), the THIRD fork-blind lane surfaced: the dispatch itself. Tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z: `pr-1591 dispatch dead-head (5/3 no-ref failures on fix/android-dap-home-sandbox) — validation_failed park`. The branch lives in the fork; `workflow_dispatch` with `ref: fix/android-dap-home-sandbox` in the base repo can never resolve → 422 "No ref found" → the gh-922 no-ref bookkeeping parks the PR — and because the park post-dates the last human push, the head-change reset never clears it. A fork PR is permanently undispatchable; every guest contribution dead-ends here.

## Root cause

`recordDispatchFailure` (js/smAgent.js:755+) treats a 422 on `ref: <branch>` as head-dead evidence — correct for same-repo PRs, structurally wrong for cross-repo PRs where the branch NEVER exists in the base repo. The dispatch contract itself (`ref: <head branch>`) assumes the branch is base-local.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Dispatch for a cross-repo PR triggers the workflow on the base default branch (or the repo's standard machine ref) with the PR number carried in inputs; the leg's checkout step resolves `refs/pull/<N>/head` (always fetchable, even when the fork branch is deleted). Same-repo PRs keep today's `ref: <branch>` dispatch (regression guard).
- **AC2** — A 422 no-ref failure on a cross-repo PR is never classified as head-dead (the head's liveness oracle for forks is `refs/pull/<N>/head`, per #1057) — no trigger-failure markers, no park accumulation.
- **AC3** — Genuinely dead fork heads (PR head ref unfetchable — fork deleted entirely) still park via the existing no-ref path, keyed to the pull-ref probe instead of the branch name.
- **AC4** — The leg's push-back path for fork PRs follows #1070's maintainer-edit contract (probe → push to fork / guest-park fallback) — no new push logic invented here.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — dispatch ref selection: fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PR → head branch (pure function, stubbed PR payloads).
- `UT-2` — no-ref classification: 422 on a fork branch name → NOT head-dead; unfetchable pull ref → head-dead (AC2/AC3).
- `IT-1` — simulated tick with a fork PR candidate: dispatch fires once, no park labels, checkout plan in the run inputs (AC1).
- `REG-1` — gh-922 bookkeeping tests (same-repo no-ref park after cap) stay green unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Running legs FROM the fork's workflow copy (untrusted code path — legs always run the base repo's workflow, checking out only the PR's data).
- Auto-merging fork PRs with failing validation (validation still required; this card only makes the legs runnable).

## References

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

# gh-1065: the title carries the LEG for every path — the dispatch input
# leg directly, and for event-path runs the strongest arming label on the
# issue (rework > review > pr_approved → review > dev). legOfRunName
# (js/common/teammateEventDedup.js) parses the trailing token, so a
# COMPLETED owner stays title-precise: the strict completed-owner leg rule
# (a leg-less completed run never swallows a KNOWN new leg) can only work
# when real leg runs carry their leg in the title.
run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && 'rework') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && 'review') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'pr_approved') && 'review') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:dev') && 'dev') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:develop') && 'dev') || github.event.label.name }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # gh-1065 (live 2026-10-18, issues #1040–#1043 / #1061): one human action
  # (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits MULTIPLE issues events and
  # each event started its own run — two per issue, three on #1061, the
  # owner hand-cancelling duplicates. The gh-1028 dedup guards the SM
  # dispatch path only; this job is the missing event-path gate. It probes
  # the repo's ai-teammate.yml runs (per-status gh api fan-out, smAgent
  # parity) and lets the `teammate` call fire only when no OLDER run for
  # the same issue + leg is in flight or freshly completed. Probe errors
  # FAIL OPEN (AC3): a broken check writes proceed=true so the only trigger
  # of a burst is never silently swallowed. The decision itself is the
  # unit-tested pure module js/common/teammateEventDedup.js (AC4) — this
  # step is transport only. The probe short-circuits BEFORE any API call
  # for workflow_dispatch (SM-side gh-1028 governs it), non-arming
  # lifecycle labels and non-teammate assignees.
  dedup:
    name: Event-path dedup probe (gh-1065)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # gh-1065 rework (review thread — gh-1029 zero-burn parity): this gate
    # MIRRORS the teammate call gate below. `on:` fires on EVERY label
    # write repo-wide, and an unguarded dedup job would allocate a runner
    # (checkout + node boot) per lifecycle-label storm — the exact burn
    # gh-1029 eliminated. Rejected events now execute ZERO jobs: the run
    # concludes failure (the gh-676 phantom pattern) and — because only

      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    outputs:
      proceed: ${{ steps.probe.outputs.proceed }}

    steps:

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: a head-targeted dispatch for a fork PR reroutes onto the base repo's standard machine ref (`main`) with the PR number and a `refs/pull/<N>/head` checkout plan in the run inputs, instead of dispatching on the fork branch which 422s forever in the base repo (live fa pr-1591). # gh-1075: [GOAL] Fork PR dispatch: trigger on base ref + checkout refs/pull/N/head — cross-repo PRs are permanently undispatchable today (live: fa #1591 re-parked after rescue)

## Description

## Goal — cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: trigger on a base ref, check out refs/pull/N/head (v1)

One sentence: **a fork PR's legs run like any other PR's legs** — the SM dispatches the workflow on a base-repo ref with the PR number as input and the leg checks out `refs/pull/<N>/head` — instead of dispatching with `ref: <fork-branch>` which 422s forever.

Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — after the dead-head park fix (#1057, merged) and the fork-aware silent-update (#1070, merged), the THIRD fork-blind lane surfaced: the dispatch itself. Tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z: `pr-1591 dispatch dead-head (5/3 no-ref failures on fix/android-dap-home-sandbox) — validation_failed park`. The branch lives in the fork; `workflow_dispatch` with `ref: fix/android-dap-home-sandbox` in the base repo can never resolve → 422 "No ref found" → the gh-922 no-ref bookkeeping parks the PR — and because the park post-dates the last human push, the head-change reset never clears it. A fork PR is permanently undispatchable; every guest contribution dead-ends here.

## Root cause

`recordDispatchFailure` (js/smAgent.js:755+) treats a 422 on `ref: <branch>` as head-dead evidence — correct for same-repo PRs, structurally wrong for cross-repo PRs where the branch NEVER exists in the base repo. The dispatch contract itself (`ref: <head branch>`) assumes the branch is base-local.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Dispatch for a cross-repo PR triggers the workflow on the base default branch (or the repo's standard machine ref) with the PR number carried in inputs; the leg's checkout step resolves `refs/pull/<N>/head` (always fetchable, even when the fork branch is deleted). Same-repo PRs keep today's `ref: <branch>` dispatch (regression guard).
- **AC2** — A 422 no-ref failure on a cross-repo PR is never classified as head-dead (the head's liveness oracle for forks is `refs/pull/<N>/head`, per #1057) — no trigger-failure markers, no park accumulation.
- **AC3** — Genuinely dead fork heads (PR head ref unfetchable — fork deleted entirely) still park via the existing no-ref path, keyed to the pull-ref probe instead of the branch name.
- **AC4** — The leg's push-back path for fork PRs follows #1070's maintainer-edit contract (probe → push to fork / guest-park fallback) — no new push logic invented here.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — dispatch ref selection: fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PR → head branch (pure function, stubbed PR payloads).
- `UT-2` — no-ref classification: 422 on a fork branch name → NOT head-dead; unfetchable pull ref → head-dead (AC2/AC3).
- `IT-1` — simulated tick with a fork PR candidate: dispatch fires once, no park labels, checkout plan in the run inputs (AC1).
- `REG-1` — gh-922 bookkeeping tests (same-repo no-ref park after cap) stay green unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Running legs FROM the fork's workflow copy (untrusted code path — legs always run the base repo's workflow, checking out only the PR's data).
- Auto-merging fork PRs with failing validation (validation still required; this card only makes the legs runnable).

## References

- Live: fa PR #1591, SM tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z ("dispatch dead-head 5/3 no-ref")
- js/smAgent.js recordDispatchFailure (:755+), js/sm/sources/githubSource.js no-ref classification (:141, :1136)
- Sibling fork-blindness cards: #1057 (park oracle — merged), #1070 (silent-update — merged), #1074 (failure observability)

+// refs/pull/<N>/head regardless of where the fork branch lives or whether
+// it still exists at all (gh-1057's oracle, now the checkout plan).

+    return 'refs/pull/' + prNumber + '/head';
+}
+
+// The head repository as an 'owner/repo' full name when (and only when)
+// the PR is CROSS-REPO. Delegates to the ONE shared gh-1070 resolver
+// (validationLiveness.forkHeadFull): case-insensitive same-repo compare
+// (config casing vs API casing must never reclassify a same-repo PR as a
+// fork), null/malformed headRepo fails closed to same-repo (the base
+// probe — a deleted fork's REST payload carries head.repo:null, exactly
+// the genuinely-dead-head shape AC3 parks through the pull-ref probe).
+function forkFullOf(item, baseOwner, baseRepo) {
+    var head = item && (item.headRepo || (item.pr && item.pr.headRepo));
+    return validationLivenessModule.forkHeadFull(head, baseOwner, baseRepo);
+}
+
+// UT-1 / AC1 — the dispatch plan for one candidate. `expandedRef` is the
+// rule's workflowRef AFTER placeholder expansion ({branch}/{prNumber});
+// `item` is the normalized source item (githubSource shape: prNumber,
+// branch, headRepo). Returns { ref, checkoutRef } — checkoutRef is null
+// whenever the plan is unchanged (same-repo PR, non-head-targeted rule,
+// missing head data), so the caller adds NO new inputs on those paths.
+function dispatchPlan(expandedRef, item, baseOwner, baseRepo) {
+    var plan = { ref: String(expandedRef == null ? '' : expandedRef), checkoutRef: null };
+    if (!item || !item.branch || !item.prNumber) return plan;
+    // Only a dispatch that TARGETED the item's head ref reroutes: a
+    // 'main'-ref (or '{prNumber}') rule dispatches where it always did.
+    if (plan.ref !== String(item.branch)) return plan;
+    if (!forkFullOf(item, baseOwner, baseRepo)) return plan; // same-repo regression guard
+    plan.ref = BASE_MACHINE_REF;
+    plan.checkoutRef = pullHeadRef(item.prNumber);
+    return plan;
+}

+// when the raw error already classified 'no-ref' (triggerFailures.
+// classifyTriggerError); `pullRefFetchable` is the refs/pull/<N>/head

+// base repo while the PR is live — only the pull ref tells the truth.
+//   'live' — fetchable: NOT head-dead; the SM records nothing (AC2).
+//   'dead' — unfetchable: the fork is gone entirely; the caller runs the
+//            existing gh-922 marker+park path keyed on the pull ref (AC3).
+function classifyForkNoRef(pullRefFetchable) {
+    return pullRefFetchable ? 'live' : 'dead';
+}

+    BASE_MACHINE_REF: BASE_MACHINE_REF,
+    pullHeadRef: pullHeadRef,
+    forkFullOf: forkFullOf,
+    dispatchPlan: dispatchPlan,
+    classifyForkNoRef: classifyForkNoRef
+};

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ### What changed
Cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: a head-targeted dispatch for a fork PR reroutes onto the base repo's standard machine ref (`main`) with the PR number and a `refs/pull/<N>/head` checkout plan in the run inputs, instead of dispatching on the fork branch which 422s forever in the base repo (live fa pr-1591). # gh-1075: [GOAL] Fork PR dispatch: trigger on base ref + checkout refs/pull/N/head — cross-repo PRs are permanently undispatchable today (live: fa #1591 re-parked after rescue)

## Description

## Goal — cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: trigger on a base ref, check out refs/pull/N/head (v1)

One sentence: **a fork PR's legs run like any other PR's legs** — the SM dispatches the workflow on a base-repo ref with the PR number as input and the leg checks out `refs/pull/<N>/head` — instead of dispatching with `ref: <fork-branch>` which 422s forever.

Live: fa PR #1591 (YuryBY fork) — after the dead-head park fix (#1057, merged) and the fork-aware silent-update (#1070, merged), the THIRD fork-blind lane surfaced: the dispatch itself. Tick 2026-10-19T06:16Z: `pr-1591 dispatch dead-head (5/3 no-ref failures on fix/android-dap-home-sandbox) — validation_failed park`. The branch lives in the fork; `workflow_dispatch` with `ref: fix/android-dap-home-sandbox` in the base repo can never resolve → 422 "No ref found" → the gh-922 no-ref bookkeeping parks the PR — and because the park post-dates the last human push, the head-change reset never clears it. A fork PR is permanently undispatchable; every guest contribution dead-ends here.

## Root cause

`recordDispatchFailure` (js/smAgent.js:755+) treats a 422 on `ref: <branch>` as head-dead evidence — correct for same-repo PRs, structurally wrong for cross-repo PRs where the branch NEVER exists in the base repo. The dispatch contract itself (`ref: <head branch>`) assumes the branch is base-local.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Dispatch for a cross-repo PR triggers the workflow on the base default branch (or the repo's standard machine ref) with the PR number carried in inputs; the leg's checkout step resolves `refs/pull/<N>/head` (always fetchable, even when the fork branch is deleted). Same-repo PRs keep today's `ref: <branch>` dispatch (regression guard).
- **AC2** — A 422 no-ref failure on a cross-repo PR is never classified as head-dead (the head's liveness oracle for forks is `refs/pull/<N>/head`, per #1057) — no trigger-failure markers, no park accumulation.
- **AC3** — Genuinely dead fork heads (PR head ref unfetchable — fork deleted entirely) still park via the existing no-ref path, keyed to the pull-ref probe instead of the branch name.
- **AC4** — The leg's push-back path for fork PRs follows #1070's maintainer-edit contract (probe → push to fork / guest-park fallback) — no new push logic invented here.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — dispatch ref selection: fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PR → head branch (pure function, stubbed PR payloads).
- `UT-2` — no-ref classification: 422 on a fork branch name → NOT head-dead; unfetchable pull ref → head-dead (AC2/AC3).
- `IT-1` — simulated tick with a fork PR candidate: dispatch fires once, no park labels, checkout plan in the run inputs (AC1).
- `REG-1` — gh-922 bookkeeping tests (same-repo no-ref park after cap) stay green unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Running legs FROM the fork's workflow copy (untrusted code path — legs always run the base repo's workflow, checking out only the PR's data).
- Auto-merging fork PRs with failing validation (validation still required; this card only makes the legs runnable).

## References
