## Summary

On v0.84.3, a `dispatch-workflow` safe-output call that includes the per-call `ref` override (landed in [#49408](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/pull/49408)) fails with a 422 from GitHub's REST API, because `ref` ends up nested inside the `inputs` object sent to `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/dispatches` instead of being passed as that endpoint's separate top-level `ref` field.

## Reproduction

Repo: `tenstorrent/tt-metal` (public), workflow `.github/workflows/silencer.md` → `silencer.lock.yml`, compiled with gh-aw v0.84.3.

- Run: https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/30792680906
- Failing job/step: https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/30792680906/job/91622304606 ("safe_outputs" / "Process Safe Outputs")
- The agent emitted a `dispatch_workflow` tool call targeting `single-card-demo-tests` with `ref: "silencer/dedupe-matmul-memconfig-mismatch-warning-77496cdc6bbbe3a9"` (its own new PR branch, from PR [[WIP] Skip ripgrep apt install when rg is already available #51894](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/pull/51894)), per the documented per-workflow dynamic-tool contract.
- Resulting log:

```
POST https://api.github.com/repos/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/workflows/single-card-demo-tests.yaml/dispatches
POST .../dispatches - 422
##[error]Failed to dispatch workflow "single-card-demo-tests": Unexpected inputs provided: ["ref"]
```

## Root cause

Per GitHub's REST API OpenAPI description (`github/rest-api-description`, `descriptions/api.github.com/api.github.com.json`, path `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/dispatches`), `ref` is a **required, top-level** field, a sibling of `inputs` — never one of the `inputs` keys.

gh-aw's per-workflow dynamic-tool `inputSchema` is generated **flat**: it adds `ref` as a property alongside the target workflow's own declared inputs (visible in our compiled lock file: the `single-card-demo-tests` dynamic tool's `inputSchema.properties` includes `build-type`, `enable-lto`, `enable-ops-recording`, `platform`, `ref`, `requested-models`, `run-perf-tests` all as siblings).

The bug is in `actions/setup/js/safe_outputs_tools_loader.cjs` (confirmed at v0.84.3 and at `main`, lines ~165–176):

```
if (hasValidWorkflowMetadataName(tool._workflow_name)) {
  const workflowName = tool._workflow_name.trim();
  tool.handler = args => {
    return handlers.defaultHandler("dispatch_workflow")({
      inputs: args,            // <-- args still contains `ref`
      workflow_name: workflowName,
    });
  };
}
```

This passes the *entire* flat `args` object (including `ref`) straight through as `inputs`, and never reads `args.ref` back out as the top-level `ref` for the `dispatch_workflow` message. Two consequences:

1. If the target workflow doesn't itself declare a `ref` input (the normal case), GitHub rejects the whole call with 422 "Unexpected inputs provided" — this is what we hit.
2. Even if a target workflow *did* declare a `ref` input (so no 422), the top-level `ref` on the `dispatch_workflow` message would be absent and silently fall back to the default ref — so the workflow would run against the wrong branch, not the one the agent intended to validate. The feature would appear to "work" but validate nothing.

## Regression history

This exact loader code path existed in v0.84.2 too, but v0.84.2's dynamic-tool schema didn't expose `ref` at all — a separate bug, [#49713](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/49713) ("per-workflow tool schema never exposes the ref parameter added in [#49408](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/pull/49408)"), which was closed as fixed on 2026-08-02. That fix added `ref` to the flat schema but didn't update the loader to strip it back out before building `inputs` — so v0.84.3 converts a previously-dormant defect into an active 422 (or silent wrong-ref dispatch).

## Suggested fix

Destructure `ref` out of `args` in the handler before building `inputs`:

```
tool.handler = args => {
  const { ref, ...inputs } = args;
  return handlers.defaultHandler("dispatch_workflow")({
    ...(ref && { ref }),
    inputs,
    workflow_name: workflowName,
  });
};
```

{"content":"# 🚨 BLOCKING: `checkout_ref` is not a declared input of the leg workflow — GitHub 422s the fork dispatch with "Unexpected inputs provided", so the fix cannot fire in production

The rerouted fork dispatch now sends `inputs.checkout_ref` (`js/smAgent.js:756`, and a backfilled `inputs.pr` at :757 when the rule carries no `{prNumber}`), but the workflow it targets declares no such input. The dispatch target is the **target repo's** `ai-teammate.yml` — every deployment of it is a copy of this repo's `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`, whose `workflow_dispatch` block declares exactly four inputs: `issue`, `leg`, `reason`, `pr` (`workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template:45-67`). A repo-wide grep confirms `checkout_ref` exists nowhere in any workflow YAML — only in `smAgent.js` and the tests.

GitHub's dispatches REST endpoint validates the `inputs` object against the workflow file's declared inputs and rejects undeclared keys with 422 "Unexpected inputs provided" — documented live in [github/gh-aw#50027](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/50027) (`Failed to dispatch workflow "…": Unexpected inputs provided: ["ref"]` on `POST …/dispatches` — 422, fixed by stripping undeclared keys before sending).

The consequence chain makes AC1 worse than unmet:

1. The dispatch no longer 422s with "No ref found" (the rerouted ref is `main`, which exists) — it 422s with "Unexpected inputs provided: ["checkout_ref"]" **on every tick**.
2. `triggerFailures.classifyTriggerError` (`js/common/triggerFailures.js:56`) only maps "no ref found"-shaped messages to `'no-ref'`; this message classifies as `'transient'`.
3. So `recordDispatchFailure` returns at the `failClass !== 'no-ref'` gate — **no probe, no markers, no park, only a console warning**. A fork PR is still permanently undispatchable, but now with zero observability — strictly worse than the gh-922 state this card fixes.

The PR description defers "leg checkout/push **consumption** of the `checkout_ref` input" as out of scope — but *declaring* the input is not consumption; without a declaration the dispatch is rejected before any leg code runs, so IT-1 ("dispatch fires once") can never hold against the real GitHub endpoint. The IT-1 test passes only because `onTrigger` is mocked and never sees GitHub's input validation.

**Fix**: declare `checkout_ref` (and document `pr`) in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`'s `workflow_dispatch` inputs (consumption can stay in the #1074 lane), and add a workflow-lint/unit assertion so a future undeclared dispatch input fails CI instead of silently 422ing. Until then, `recommendation` stays REQUEST_CHANGES.

## Summary

On v0.84.3, a `dispatch-workflow` safe-output call that includes the per-call `ref` override (landed in [#49408](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/pull/49408)) fails with a 422 from GitHub's REST API, because `ref` ends up nested inside the `inputs` object sent to `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/dispatches` instead of being passed as that endpoint's separate top-level `ref` field.

## Reproduction

Repo: `tenstorrent/tt-metal` (public), workflow `.github/workflows/silencer.md` → `silencer.lock.yml`, compiled with gh-aw v0.84.3.

- Run: https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/30792680906
- Failing job/step: https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/30792680906/job/91622304606 ("safe_outputs" / "Process Safe Outputs")
- The agent emitted a `dispatch_workflow` tool call targeting `single-card-demo-tests` with `ref: "silencer/dedupe-matmul-memconfig-mismatch-warning-77496cdc6bbbe3a9"` (its own new PR branch, from PR [[WIP] Skip ripgrep apt install when rg is already available #51894](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/pull/51894)), per the documented per-workflow dynamic-tool contract.
- Resulting log:

```
POST https://api.github.com/repos/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/workflows/single-card-demo-tests.yaml/dispatches
POST .../dispatches - 422
##[error]Failed to dispatch workflow "single-card-demo-tests": Unexpected inputs provided: ["ref"]
```

## Root cause

Per GitHub's REST API OpenAPI description (`github/rest-api-description`, `descriptions/api.github.com/api.github.com.json`, path `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/dispatches`), `ref` is a **required, top-level** field, a sibling of `inputs` — never one of the `inputs` keys.

gh-aw's per-workflow dynamic-tool `inputSchema` is generated **flat**: it adds `ref` as a property alongside the target workflow's own declared inputs (visible in our compiled lock file: the `single-card-demo-tests` dynamic tool's `inputSchema.properties` includes `build-type`, `enable-lto`, `enable-ops-recording`, `platform`, `ref`, `requested-models`, `run-perf-tests` all as siblings).

The bug is in `actions/setup/js/safe_outputs_tools_loader.cjs` (confirmed at v0.84.3 and at `main`, lines ~165–176):

```
if (hasValidWorkflowMetadataName(tool._workflow_name)) {
  const workflowName = tool._workflow_name.trim();
  tool.handler = args => {
    return handlers.defaultHandler("dispatch_workflow")({
      inputs: args,            // <-- args still contains `ref`
      workflow_name: workflowName,
    });
  };
}
```

This passes the *entire* flat `args` object (including `ref`) straight through as `inputs`, and never reads `args.ref` back out as the top-level `ref` for the `dispatch_workflow` message. Two consequences:

1. If the target workflow doesn't itself declare a `ref` input (the normal case), GitHub rejects the whole call with 422 "Unexpected inputs provided" — this is what we hit.
2. Even if a target workflow *did* declare a `ref` input (so no 422), the top-level `ref` on the `dispatch_workflow` message would be absent and silently fall back to the default ref — so the workflow would run against the wrong branch, not the one the agent intended to validate. The feature would appear to "work" but validate nothing.

## Regression history

This exact loader code path existed in v0.84.2 too, but v0.84.2's dynamic-tool schema didn't expose `ref` at all — a separate bug, [#49713](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/49713) ("per-workflow tool schema never exposes the ref parameter added in [#49408](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/pull/49408)"), which was closed as fixed on 2026-08-02. That fix added `ref` to the flat schema but didn't update the loader to strip it back out before building `inputs` — so v0.84.3 converts a previously-dormant defect into an active 422 (or silent wrong-ref dispatch).

## Suggested fix

Destructure `ref` out of `args` in the handler before building `inputs`:

```
tool.handler = args => {
  const { ref, ...inputs } = args;
  return handlers.defaultHandler("dispatch_workflow")({
    ...(ref && { ref }),
    inputs,
    workflow_name: workflowName,
  });
};
```

The rerouted fork dispatch now sends `inputs.checkout_ref` (`js/smAgent.js:756`, and a backfilled `inputs.pr` at :757 when the rule carries no `{prNumber}`), but the workflow it targets declares no such input. The dispatch target is the **target repo's** `ai-teammate.yml` — every deployment of it is a copy of this repo's `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`, whose `workflow_dispatch` block declares exactly four inputs: `issue`, `leg`, `reason`, `pr` (`workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template:45-67`). A repo-wide grep confirms `checkout_ref` exists nowhere in any workflow YAML — only in `smAgent.js` and the tests.

GitHub's dispatches REST endpoint validates the `inputs` object against the workflow file's declared inputs and rejects undeclared keys with 422 "Unexpected inputs provided" — documented live in [github/gh-aw#50027](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/50027) (`Failed to dispatch workflow "…": Unexpected inputs provided: ["ref"]` on `POST …/dispatches` — 422, fixed by stripping undeclared keys before sending).

The consequence chain makes AC1 worse than unmet:

1. The dispatch no longer 422s with "No ref found" (the rerouted ref is `main`, which exists) — it 422s with "Unexpected inputs provided: ["checkout_ref"]" **on every tick**.
2. `triggerFailures.classifyTriggerError` (`js/common/triggerFailures.js:56`) only maps "no ref found"-shaped messages to `'no-ref'`; this message classifies as `'transient'`.
3. So `recordDispatchFailure` returns at the `failClass !== 'no-ref'` gate — **no probe, no markers, no park, only a console warning**. A fork PR is still permanently undispatchable, but now with zero observability — strictly worse than the gh-922 state this card fixes.

The PR description defers "leg checkout/push **consumption** of the `checkout_ref` input" as out of scope — but *declaring* the input is not consumption; without a declaration the dispatch is rejected before any leg code runs, so IT-1 ("dispatch fires once") can never hold against the real GitHub endpoint. The IT-1 test passes only because `onTrigger` is mocked and never sees GitHub's input validation.

**Fix**: declare `checkout_ref` (and document `pr`) in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`'s `workflow_dispatch` inputs (consumption can stay in the #1074 lane), and add a workflow-lint/unit assertion so a future undeclared dispatch input fails CI instead of silently 422ing. Until then, `recommendation` stays REQUEST_CHANGES.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the gh-1028 single-writer leg guard is blind for rerouted fork dispatches — the run's `head_branch` is now `main`, not the fork branch

`headRefDispatch` preserves the guard's firing condition, but the guard's probe key — `it0.branch`, the fork branch name — no longer matches anything in the run list once the dispatch is rerouted. A `workflow_dispatch` run's `head_branch` is the dispatch ref (`main` after this PR), while `hasActiveLegRunOnBranch` still asks for runs whose `head_branch IS the dispatch branch` (`js/smAgent.js:678` → `:397` → `branchLegGuardModule.hasActiveLegRunOnBranch(runs, branch, …)`).

So for a fork PR the gh-1028 suppression can never see an in-flight leg: if both rework arms match the same fork PR (the issue-anchored rework-on-red-ci and the PR-anchored rework-on-label, exactly the gh-1028 live pathology on PR #1017), both dispatch, and two rework legs race the same fork head — with #1070 maintainer-edit pushes landing in the *fork*, the same double-push race gh-1028 was built to prevent. (Pre-gh-1075 this was latent because fork dispatches always 422'd; once the dispatch blocker is fixed this becomes live.)

Please key the probe on the pull ref (or `pr-<N>`) when `forkPlan.checkoutRef` is set — e.g. pass `forkPlan.checkoutRef || it0.branch` to `hasActiveLegRunOnBranch` — and add a regression test: fork PR + one in-flight leg run whose `head_branch` is `main` + a second dispatch arm → suppressed.

{"content":"# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the pull-ref liveness probe is unauthenticated — on private base repos it always fails closed to "live" and AC3 parking silently never fires

`forkPullRefLive` probes `git ls-remote https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git refs/pull/<N>/head` with no credentials (`js/smAgent.js:848`). For a private base repo (the common case for machine targets) this errors with "Repository not found" on every probe; the catch then returns `true` (fail-open, per the gh-922 blind-tick invariant) — so a genuinely dead fork head on a private repo is **never** classified 'dead', never accumulates markers, never parks. AC3 ("genuinely dead fork heads still park") is silently void exactly where most of the fleet runs.

The rest of this codebase probes the *runner's authenticated remote* instead of a hardcoded public URL: `js/prepareTestPRForReview.js:214` (`git ls-remote --heads origin …`), `js/prepareCliTestReworkSetup.js:106`, `js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js:81` — the SM runs in a checkout of the base repo where `origin` already carries the token (cf. the `GH_TOKEN` push-URL handling at `js/smAgent.js:2037`).

**Fix**: probe `origin` (or a token-bearing URL assembled from split literals the way the existing push URLs are, so the token never appears contiguously in source): `git ls-remote origin refs/pull/<N>/head`. Keep the fail-open catch as-is. A unit test with a private-repo-shaped probe error (auth failure) asserting "never parks but logs a distinct degraded warning" would pin the intent.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the "fork deleted entirely" shape (`headRepo: null`) never reaches the pull-ref probe — the doc comment and the AC3 "keyed on the pull ref" claim don't hold for it

`forkDispatch.forkFullOf` fails closed to same-repo when `headRepo` is null, and the module comment (`js/common/forkDispatch.js:47-53`) names exactly that shape — "a deleted fork's REST payload carries head.repo:null" — as what "parks through the pull-ref probe". But with `headRepo` null the probe path here is **unreachable**:

1. `dispatchPlan` also sees `forkFullOf === null` → the plan is **not** rerouted → the dispatch still targets the fork branch → 422 "No ref found for: <fork-branch>".
2. Back in `recordDispatchFailure`, `forkFullOf(item, …)` is again null → the code drops to the same-repo branch (`js/smAgent.js:836`) → `expandedRef === item.branch` holds → `recordNoRefBookkeeping` keys the marker/park on the **branch name**, and no `ls-remote` probe ever runs.

So for the deleted-fork shape the AC3 outcome (a park) still happens — but through the pre-gh-1075 branch-keyed path, not "the existing no-ref path, keyed on the pull ref" as AC3 and the PR description state, and with no test coverage (every AC3 test keeps `headRepo: FORK_FULL` populated). Two consistency asks:

- Either route the null-`headRepo` + no-ref shape into the pull-ref probe (e.g. when `expandedRef === item.branch` and the branch is unfetchable on the base remote, treat as fork-suspect and probe `refs/pull/<N>/head`) — this also fixes a side effect: with the plan un-rerouted, a fork branch whose name collides with an existing base branch would dispatch on the *base* branch and validate the wrong code;
- or fix the comment/PR description/tests to state that the pull-ref-keyed park covers only the populated-`headRepo` case and the deleted-fork case parks branch-keyed via the legacy path.

Not blocking — parking still occurs — but the contract text and the tests currently describe a probe path the deleted-fork shape cannot reach.

## Summary

On v0.84.3, a `dispatch-workflow` safe-output call that includes the per-call `ref` override (landed in [#49408](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/pull/49408)) fails with a 422 from GitHub's REST API, because `ref` ends up nested inside the `inputs` object sent to `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/dispatches` instead of being passed as that endpoint's separate top-level `ref` field.

## Reproduction

Repo: `tenstorrent/tt-metal` (public), workflow `.github/workflows/silencer.md` → `silencer.lock.yml`, compiled with gh-aw v0.84.3.

- Run: https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/30792680906
- Failing job/step: https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/30792680906/job/91622304606 ("safe_outputs" / "Process Safe Outputs")
- The agent emitted a `dispatch_workflow` tool call targeting `single-card-demo-tests` with `ref: "silencer/dedupe-matmul-memconfig-mismatch-warning-77496cdc6bbbe3a9"` (its own new PR branch, from PR [[WIP] Skip ripgrep apt install when rg is already available #51894](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/pull/51894)), per the documented per-workflow dynamic-tool contract.
- Resulting log:

```
POST https://api.github.com/repos/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/workflows/single-card-demo-tests.yaml/dispatches
POST .../dispatches - 422
##[error]Failed to dispatch workflow "single-card-demo-tests": Unexpected inputs provided: ["ref"]
```

## Root cause

Per GitHub's REST API OpenAPI description (`github/rest-api-description`, `descriptions/api.github.com/api.github.com.json`, path `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/dispatches`), `ref` is a **required, top-level** field, a sibling of `inputs` — never one of the `inputs` keys.

gh-aw's per-workflow dynamic-tool `inputSchema` is generated **flat**: it adds `ref` as a property alongside the target workflow's own declared inputs (visible in our compiled lock file: the `single-card-demo-tests` dynamic tool's `inputSchema.properties` includes `build-type`, `enable-lto`, `enable-ops-recording`, `platform`, `ref`, `requested-models`, `run-perf-tests` all as siblings).

The bug is in `actions/setup/js/safe_outputs_tools_loader.cjs` (confirmed at v0.84.3 and at `main`, lines ~165–176):

```
if (hasValidWorkflowMetadataName(tool._workflow_name)) {
  const workflowName = tool._workflow_name.trim();
  tool.handler = args => {
    return handlers.defaultHandler("dispatch_workflow")({
      inputs: args,            // <-- args still contains `ref`
      workflow_name: workflowName,
    });
  };
}
```

This passes the *entire* flat `args` object (including `ref`) straight through as `inputs`, and never reads `args.ref` back out as the top-level `ref` for the `dispatch_workflow` message. Two consequences:

1. If the target workflow doesn't itself declare a `ref` input (the normal case), GitHub rejects the whole call with 422 "Unexpected inputs provided" — this is what we hit.
2. Even if a target workflow *did* declare a `ref` input (so no 422), the top-level `ref` on the `dispatch_workflow` message would be absent and silently fall back to the default ref — so the workflow would run against the wrong branch, not the one the agent intended to validate. The feature would appear to "work" but validate nothing.

## Regression history

This exact loader code path existed in v0.84.2 too, but v0.84.2's dynamic-tool schema didn't expose `ref` at all — a separate bug, [#49713](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/49713) ("per-workflow tool schema never exposes the ref parameter added in [#49408](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/pull/49408)"), which was closed as fixed on 2026-08-02. That fix added `ref` to the flat schema but didn't update the loader to strip it back out before building `inputs` — so v0.84.3 converts a previously-dormant defect into an active 422 (or silent wrong-ref dispatch).

## Suggested fix

Destructure `ref` out of `args` in the handler before building `inputs`:

```
tool.handler = args => {
  const { ref, ...inputs } = args;
  return handlers.defaultHandler("dispatch_workflow")({
    ...(ref && { ref }),
    inputs,
    workflow_name: workflowName,
  });
};
```

GitHub's dispatches REST endpoint validates the `inputs` object against the workflow file's declared inputs and rejects undeclared keys with 422 "Unexpected inputs provided" — documented live in [github/gh-aw#50027](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/50027) (`Failed to dispatch workflow "…": Unexpected inputs provided: ["ref"]` on `POST …/dispatches` — 422, fixed by stripping undeclared keys before sending).

## Summary

On v0.84.3, a `dispatch-workflow` safe-output call that includes the per-call `ref` override (landed in [#49408](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/pull/49408)) fails with a 422 from GitHub's REST API, because `ref` ends up nested inside the `inputs` object sent to `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/dispatches` instead of being passed as that endpoint's separate top-level `ref` field.

## Reproduction

Repo: `tenstorrent/tt-metal` (public), workflow `.github/workflows/silencer.md` → `silencer.lock.yml`, compiled with gh-aw v0.84.3.

- Run: https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/30792680906
- Failing job/step: https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/30792680906/job/91622304606 ("safe_outputs" / "Process Safe Outputs")
- The agent emitted a `dispatch_workflow` tool call targeting `single-card-demo-tests` with `ref: "silencer/dedupe-matmul-memconfig-mismatch-warning-77496cdc6bbbe3a9"` (its own new PR branch, from PR [[WIP] Skip ripgrep apt install when rg is already available #51894](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/pull/51894)), per the documented per-workflow dynamic-tool contract.
- Resulting log:

```
POST https://api.github.com/repos/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/workflows/single-card-demo-tests.yaml/dispatches
POST .../dispatches - 422
##[error]Failed to dispatch workflow "single-card-demo-tests": Unexpected inputs provided: ["ref"]
```

## Root cause

Per GitHub's REST API OpenAPI description (`github/rest-api-description`, `descriptions/api.github.com/api.github.com.json`, path `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/dispatches`), `ref` is a **required, top-level** field, a sibling of `inputs` — never one of the `inputs` keys.

gh-aw's per-workflow dynamic-tool `inputSchema` is generated **flat**: it adds `ref` as a property alongside the target workflow's own declared inputs (visible in our compiled lock file: the `single-card-demo-tests` dynamic tool's `inputSchema.properties` includes `build-type`, `enable-lto`, `enable-ops-recording`, `platform`, `ref`, `requested-models`, `run-perf-tests` all as siblings).

The bug is in `actions/setup/js/safe_outputs_tools_loader.cjs` (confirmed at v0.84.3 and at `main`, lines ~165–176):

```
if (hasValidWorkflowMetadataName(tool._workflow_name)) {
  const workflowName = tool._workflow_name.trim();
  tool.handler = args => {
    return handlers.defaultHandler("dispatch_workflow")({
      inputs: args,            // <-- args still contains `ref`
      workflow_name: workflowName,
    });
  };
}
```

This passes the *entire* flat `args` object (including `ref`) straight through as `inputs`, and never reads `args.ref` back out as the top-level `ref` for the `dispatch_workflow` message. Two consequences:

1. If the target workflow doesn't itself declare a `ref` input (the normal case), GitHub rejects the whole call with 422 "Unexpected inputs provided" — this is what we hit.
2. Even if a target workflow *did* declare a `ref` input (so no 422), the top-level `ref` on the `dispatch_workflow` message would be absent and silently fall back to the default ref — so the workflow would run against the wrong branch, not the one the agent intended to validate. The feature would appear to "work" but validate nothing.

## Regression history

This exact loader code path existed in v0.84.2 too, but v0.84.2's dynamic-tool schema didn't expose `ref` at all — a separate bug, [#49713](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/49713) ("per-workflow tool schema never exposes the ref parameter added in [#49408](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/pull/49408)"), which was closed as fixed on 2026-08-02. That fix added `ref` to the flat schema but didn't update the loader to strip it back out before building `inputs` — so v0.84.3 converts a previously-dormant defect into an active 422 (or silent wrong-ref dispatch).

## Suggested fix

Destructure `ref` out of `args` in the handler before building `inputs`:

```
tool.handler = args => {
  const { ref, ...inputs } = args;
  return handlers.defaultHandler("dispatch_workflow")({
    ...(ref && { ref }),
    inputs,
    workflow_name: workflowName,
  });
};
```

{"content":"# 🚨 BLOCKING: `checkout_ref` is not a declared input of the leg workflow — GitHub 422s the fork dispatch with "Unexpected inputs provided", so the fix cannot fire in production

The rerouted fork dispatch now sends `inputs.checkout_ref` (`js/smAgent.js:756`, and a backfilled `inputs.pr` at :757 when the rule carries no `{prNumber}`), but the workflow it targets declares no such input. The dispatch target is the **target repo's** `ai-teammate.yml` — every deployment of it is a copy of this repo's `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`, whose `workflow_dispatch` block declares exactly four inputs: `issue`, `leg`, `reason`, `pr` (`workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template:45-67`). A repo-wide grep confirms `checkout_ref` exists nowhere in any workflow YAML — only in `smAgent.js` and the tests.

GitHub's dispatches REST endpoint validates the `inputs` object against the workflow file's declared inputs and rejects undeclared keys with 422 "Unexpected inputs provided" — documented live in [github/gh-aw#50027](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/50027) (`Failed to dispatch workflow "…": Unexpected inputs provided: ["ref"]` on `POST …/dispatches` — 422, fixed by stripping undeclared keys before sending).

The consequence chain makes AC1 worse than unmet:

1. The dispatch no longer 422s with "No ref found" (the rerouted ref is `main`, which exists) — it 422s with "Unexpected inputs provided: ["checkout_ref"]" **on every tick**.
2. `triggerFailures.classifyTriggerError` (`js/common/triggerFailures.js:56`) only maps "no ref found"-shaped messages to `'no-ref'`; this message classifies as `'transient'`.
3. So `recordDispatchFailure` returns at the `failClass !== 'no-ref'` gate — **no probe, no markers, no park, only a console warning**. A fork PR is still permanently undispatchable, but now with zero observability — strictly worse than the gh-922 state this card fixes.

The PR description defers "leg checkout/push **consumption** of the `checkout_ref` input" as out of scope — but *declaring* the input is not consumption; without a declaration the dispatch is rejected before any leg code runs, so IT-1 ("dispatch fires once") can never hold against the real GitHub endpoint. The IT-1 test passes only because `onTrigger` is mocked and never sees GitHub's input validation.

**Fix**: declare `checkout_ref` (and document `pr`) in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`'s `workflow_dispatch` inputs (consumption can stay in the #1074 lane), and add a workflow-lint/unit assertion so a future undeclared dispatch input fails CI instead of silently 422ing. Until then, `recommendation` stays REQUEST_CHANGES.

{"content":"# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the pull-ref liveness probe is unauthenticated — on private base repos it always fails closed to "live" and AC3 parking silently never fires

`forkPullRefLive` probes `git ls-remote https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git refs/pull/<N>/head` with no credentials (`js/smAgent.js:848`). {"content":"# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the "fork deleted entirely" shape (`headRepo: null`) never reaches the pull-ref probe — the doc comment and the AC3 "keyed on the pull ref" claim don't hold for it

1. `dispatchPlan` also sees `forkFullOf === null` → the plan is **not** rerouted → the dispatch still targets the fork branch → 422 "No ref found for: <fork-branch>".

## Summary

On v0.84.3, a `dispatch-workflow` safe-output call that includes the per-call `ref` override (landed in [#49408](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/pull/49408)) fails with a 422 from GitHub's REST API, because `ref` ends up nested inside the `inputs` object sent to `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/dispatches` instead of being passed as that endpoint's separate top-level `ref` field.

## Reproduction

Repo: `tenstorrent/tt-metal` (public), workflow `.github/workflows/silencer.md` → `silencer.lock.yml`, compiled with gh-aw v0.84.3.

- Run: https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/30792680906
- Failing job/step: https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/30792680906/job/91622304606 ("safe_outputs" / "Process Safe Outputs")
- The agent emitted a `dispatch_workflow` tool call targeting `single-card-demo-tests` with `ref: "silencer/dedupe-matmul-memconfig-mismatch-warning-77496cdc6bbbe3a9"` (its own new PR branch, from PR [[WIP] Skip ripgrep apt install when rg is already available #51894](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/pull/51894)), per the documented per-workflow dynamic-tool contract.
- Resulting log:

```
POST https://api.github.com/repos/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/workflows/single-card-demo-tests.yaml/dispatches
POST .../dispatches - 422
##[error]Failed to dispatch workflow "single-card-demo-tests": Unexpected inputs provided: ["ref"]
```

## Root cause

Per GitHub's REST API OpenAPI description (`github/rest-api-description`, `descriptions/api.github.com/api.github.com.json`, path `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/dispatches`), `ref` is a **required, top-level** field, a sibling of `inputs` — never one of the `inputs` keys.

gh-aw's per-workflow dynamic-tool `inputSchema` is generated **flat**: it adds `ref` as a property alongside the target workflow's own declared inputs (visible in our compiled lock file: the `single-card-demo-tests` dynamic tool's `inputSchema.properties` includes `build-type`, `enable-lto`, `enable-ops-recording`, `platform`, `ref`, `requested-models`, `run-perf-tests` all as siblings).

The bug is in `actions/setup/js/safe_outputs_tools_loader.cjs` (confirmed at v0.84.3 and at `main`, lines ~165–176):

```
if (hasValidWorkflowMetadataName(tool._workflow_name)) {
  const workflowName = tool._workflow_name.trim();
  tool.handler = args => {
    return handlers.defaultHandler("dispatch_workflow")({
      inputs: args,            // <-- args still contains `ref`
      workflow_name: workflowName,
    });
  };
}
```

This passes the *entire* flat `args` object (including `ref`) straight through as `inputs`, and never reads `args.ref` back out as the top-level `ref` for the `dispatch_workflow` message. Two consequences:

1. If the target workflow doesn't itself declare a `ref` input (the normal case), GitHub rejects the whole call with 422 "Unexpected inputs provided" — this is what we hit.
2. Even if a target workflow *did* declare a `ref` input (so no 422), the top-level `ref` on the `dispatch_workflow` message would be absent and silently fall back to the default ref — so the workflow would run against the wrong branch, not the one the agent intended to validate. The feature would appear to "work" but validate nothing.

## Regression history

This exact loader code path existed in v0.84.2 too, but v0.84.2's dynamic-tool schema didn't expose `ref` at all — a separate bug, [#49713](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/49713) ("per-workflow tool schema never exposes the ref parameter added in [#49408](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/pull/49408)"), which was closed as fixed on 2026-08-02. That fix added `ref` to the flat schema but didn't update the loader to strip it back out before building `inputs` — so v0.84.3 converts a previously-dormant defect into an active 422 (or silent wrong-ref dispatch).

## Suggested fix

Destructure `ref` out of `args` in the handler before building `inputs`:

```
tool.handler = args => {
  const { ref, ...inputs } = args;
  return handlers.defaultHandler("dispatch_workflow")({
    ...(ref && { ref }),
    inputs,
    workflow_name: workflowName,
  });
};
```

{"content":"# 🚨 BLOCKING: `checkout_ref` is not a declared input of the leg workflow — GitHub 422s the fork dispatch with "Unexpected inputs provided", so the fix cannot fire in production

The rerouted fork dispatch now sends `inputs.checkout_ref` (`js/smAgent.js:756`, and a backfilled `inputs.pr` at :757 when the rule carries no `{prNumber}`), but the workflow it targets declares no such input. The dispatch target is the **target repo's** `ai-teammate.yml` — every deployment of it is a copy of this repo's `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`, whose `workflow_dispatch` block declares exactly four inputs: `issue`, `leg`, `reason`, `pr` (`workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template:45-67`). A repo-wide grep confirms `checkout_ref` exists nowhere in any workflow YAML — only in `smAgent.js` and the tests.

GitHub's dispatches REST endpoint validates the `inputs` object against the workflow file's declared inputs and rejects undeclared keys with 422 "Unexpected inputs provided" — documented live in [github/gh-aw#50027](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/50027) (`Failed to dispatch workflow "…": Unexpected inputs provided: ["ref"]` on `POST …/dispatches` — 422, fixed by stripping undeclared keys before sending).

The consequence chain makes AC1 worse than unmet:

1. The dispatch no longer 422s with "No ref found" (the rerouted ref is `main`, which exists) — it 422s with "Unexpected inputs provided: ["checkout_ref"]" **on every tick**.
2. `triggerFailures.classifyTriggerError` (`js/common/triggerFailures.js:56`) only maps "no ref found"-shaped messages to `'no-ref'`; this message classifies as `'transient'`.
3. So `recordDispatchFailure` returns at the `failClass !== 'no-ref'` gate — **no probe, no markers, no park, only a console warning**. A fork PR is still permanently undispatchable, but now with zero observability — strictly worse than the gh-922 state this card fixes.

The PR description defers "leg checkout/push **consumption** of the `checkout_ref` input" as out of scope — but *declaring* the input is not consumption; without a declaration the dispatch is rejected before any leg code runs, so IT-1 ("dispatch fires once") can never hold against the real GitHub endpoint. The IT-1 test passes only because `onTrigger` is mocked and never sees GitHub's input validation.

**Fix**: declare `checkout_ref` (and document `pr`) in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`'s `workflow_dispatch` inputs (consumption can stay in the #1074 lane), and add a workflow-lint/unit assertion so a future undeclared dispatch input fails CI instead of silently 422ing. Until then, `recommendation` stays REQUEST_CHANGES.

{"content":"# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the pull-ref liveness probe is unauthenticated — on private base repos it always fails closed to "live" and AC3 parking silently never fires

`forkPullRefLive` probes `git ls-remote https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git refs/pull/<N>/head` with no credentials (`js/smAgent.js:848`). For a private base repo (the common case for machine targets) this errors with "Repository not found" on every probe; the catch then returns `true` (fail-open, per the gh-922 blind-tick invariant) — so a genuinely dead fork head on a private repo is **never** classified 'dead', never accumulates markers, never parks. AC3 ("genuinely dead fork heads still park") is silently void exactly where most of the fleet runs.

The rest of this codebase probes the *runner's authenticated remote* instead of a hardcoded public URL: `js/prepareTestPRForReview.js:214` (`git ls-remote --heads origin …`), `js/prepareCliTestReworkSetup.js:106`, `js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js:81` — the SM runs in a checkout of the base repo where `origin` already carries the token (cf. the `GH_TOKEN` push-URL handling at `js/smAgent.js:2037`).

**Fix**: probe `origin` (or a token-bearing URL assembled from split literals the way the existing push URLs are, so the token never appears contiguously in source): `git ls-remote origin refs/pull/<N>/head`. Keep the fail-open catch as-is. A unit test with a private-repo-shaped probe error (auth failure) asserting "never parks but logs a distinct degraded warning" would pin the intent.

{"content":"# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the "fork deleted entirely" shape (`headRepo: null`) never reaches the pull-ref probe — the doc comment and the AC3 "keyed on the pull ref" claim don't hold for it

## Summary

On v0.84.3, a `dispatch-workflow` safe-output call that includes the per-call `ref` override (landed in [#49408](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/pull/49408)) fails with a 422 from GitHub's REST API, because `ref` ends up nested inside the `inputs` object sent to `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/dispatches` instead of being passed as that endpoint's separate top-level `ref` field.

## Reproduction

Repo: `tenstorrent/tt-metal` (public), workflow `.github/workflows/silencer.md` → `silencer.lock.yml`, compiled with gh-aw v0.84.3.

- Run: https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/30792680906
- Failing job/step: https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/runs/30792680906/job/91622304606 ("safe_outputs" / "Process Safe Outputs")
- The agent emitted a `dispatch_workflow` tool call targeting `single-card-demo-tests` with `ref: "silencer/dedupe-matmul-memconfig-mismatch-warning-77496cdc6bbbe3a9"` (its own new PR branch, from PR [[WIP] Skip ripgrep apt install when rg is already available #51894](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/pull/51894)), per the documented per-workflow dynamic-tool contract.
- Resulting log:

```
POST https://api.github.com/repos/tenstorrent/tt-metal/actions/workflows/single-card-demo-tests.yaml/dispatches
POST .../dispatches - 422
##[error]Failed to dispatch workflow "single-card-demo-tests": Unexpected inputs provided: ["ref"]
```

## Root cause

Per GitHub's REST API OpenAPI description (`github/rest-api-description`, `descriptions/api.github.com/api.github.com.json`, path `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/dispatches`), `ref` is a **required, top-level** field, a sibling of `inputs` — never one of the `inputs` keys.

gh-aw's per-workflow dynamic-tool `inputSchema` is generated **flat**: it adds `ref` as a property alongside the target workflow's own declared inputs (visible in our compiled lock file: the `single-card-demo-tests` dynamic tool's `inputSchema.properties` includes `build-type`, `enable-lto`, `enable-ops-recording`, `platform`, `ref`, `requested-models`, `run-perf-tests` all as siblings).

The bug is in `actions/setup/js/safe_outputs_tools_loader.cjs` (confirmed at v0.84.3 and at `main`, lines ~165–176):

```
if (hasValidWorkflowMetadataName(tool._workflow_name)) {
  const workflowName = tool._workflow_name.trim();
  tool.handler = args => {
    return handlers.defaultHandler("dispatch_workflow")({
      inputs: args,            // <-- args still contains `ref`
      workflow_name: workflowName,
    });
  };
}
```

This passes the *entire* flat `args` object (including `ref`) straight through as `inputs`, and never reads `args.ref` back out as the top-level `ref` for the `dispatch_workflow` message. Two consequences:

1. If the target workflow doesn't itself declare a `ref` input (the normal case), GitHub rejects the whole call with 422 "Unexpected inputs provided" — this is what we hit.
2. Even if a target workflow *did* declare a `ref` input (so no 422), the top-level `ref` on the `dispatch_workflow` message would be absent and silently fall back to the default ref — so the workflow would run against the wrong branch, not the one the agent intended to validate. The feature would appear to "work" but validate nothing.

## Regression history

This exact loader code path existed in v0.84.2 too, but v0.84.2's dynamic-tool schema didn't expose `ref` at all — a separate bug, [#49713](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/49713) ("per-workflow tool schema never exposes the ref parameter added in [#49408](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/pull/49408)"), which was closed as fixed on 2026-08-02. That fix added `ref` to the flat schema but didn't update the loader to strip it back out before building `inputs` — so v0.84.3 converts a previously-dormant defect into an active 422 (or silent wrong-ref dispatch).

## Suggested fix

Destructure `ref` out of `args` in the handler before building `inputs`:

```
tool.handler = args => {
  const { ref, ...inputs } = args;
  return handlers.defaultHandler("dispatch_workflow")({
    ...(ref && { ref }),
    inputs,
    workflow_name: workflowName,
  });
};
```

{"content":"# 🚨 BLOCKING: `checkout_ref` is not a declared input of the leg workflow — GitHub 422s the fork dispatch with "Unexpected inputs provided", so the fix cannot fire in production

The rerouted fork dispatch now sends `inputs.checkout_ref` (`js/smAgent.js:756`, and a backfilled `inputs.pr` at :757 when the rule carries no `{prNumber}`), but the workflow it targets declares no such input. The dispatch target is the **target repo's** `ai-teammate.yml` — every deployment of it is a copy of this repo's `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`, whose `workflow_dispatch` block declares exactly four inputs: `issue`, `leg`, `reason`, `pr` (`workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template:45-67`). A repo-wide grep confirms `checkout_ref` exists nowhere in any workflow YAML — only in `smAgent.js` and the tests.

GitHub's dispatches REST endpoint validates the `inputs` object against the workflow file's declared inputs and rejects undeclared keys with 422 "Unexpected inputs provided" — documented live in [github/gh-aw#50027](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/50027) (`Failed to dispatch workflow "…": Unexpected inputs provided: ["ref"]` on `POST …/dispatches` — 422, fixed by stripping undeclared keys before sending).

The consequence chain makes AC1 worse than unmet:

1. The dispatch no longer 422s with "No ref found" (the rerouted ref is `main`, which exists) — it 422s with "Unexpected inputs provided: ["checkout_ref"]" **on every tick**.
2. `triggerFailures.classifyTriggerError` (`js/common/triggerFailures.js:56`) only maps "no ref found"-shaped messages to `'no-ref'`; this message classifies as `'transient'`.
3. So `recordDispatchFailure` returns at the `failClass !== 'no-ref'` gate — **no probe, no markers, no park, only a console warning**. A fork PR is still permanently undispatchable, but now with zero observability — strictly worse than the gh-922 state this card fixes.

The PR description defers "leg checkout/push **consumption** of the `checkout_ref` input" as out of scope — but *declaring* the input is not consumption; without a declaration the dispatch is rejected before any leg code runs, so IT-1 ("dispatch fires once") can never hold against the real GitHub endpoint. The IT-1 test passes only because `onTrigger` is mocked and never sees GitHub's input validation.

**Fix**: declare `checkout_ref` (and document `pr`) in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`'s `workflow_dispatch` inputs (consumption can stay in the #1074 lane), and add a workflow-lint/unit assertion so a future undeclared dispatch input fails CI instead of silently 422ing. Until then, `recommendation` stays REQUEST_CHANGES.

## Review complete — `REQUEST_CHANGES` (1 BLOCKING, 4 IMPORTANT, 1 SUGGESTION)

**🚨 Blocker — the fix cannot fire in production.** The rerouted fork dispatch sends `inputs.checkout_ref` (`js/smAgent.js:756`), but the leg workflow it targets declares no such input — `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template:45-67` declares only `issue`/`leg`/`reason`/`pr`, and repo-wide grep shows `checkout_ref` in no workflow YAML. Fork PRs stay permanently undispatchable — now silently. Declaring the input is not the deferred "consumption" work; without it the dispatch is rejected before any leg runs.

**⚠️ Important findings:**
- `js/smAgent.js:678` — the gh-1028 single-writer leg guard probes the fork branch name, but rerouted runs have `head_branch = main` → guard never matches; two rework arms can double-dispatch on a fork head (the PR #1017 race, now with fork pushes).

- `js/smAgent.js:820` — the deleted-fork shape (`headRepo:null`, named in the module's own comment) never reaches the pull-ref probe: no reroute in `dispatchPlan` either, so it 422s on the branch and parks *branch-keyed* via the legacy path — contradicting AC3/"keyed on the pull ref" and untested.
- `js/smAgent.js:825` — the shared `recordDispatchFailure` also serves the un-rerouted `validate_pr` CI lane (`:3411`), whose structural fork 422s are now fully silenced; validation can never arm for fork PRs with zero trace.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md — detailed inline comment files"] O4["Always reference inline comment files via the 'comment' field — do NOT use inline 'body'"] O5["Inline comments MUST use a line number that exists in the PR diff"] O6["If a finding is on unchanged code outside the diff, put it in outputs/pr_review_general.md instead"] O1 --> O2 --> O3 --> O4 --> O5 --> O6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief Markdown summary, under 20 lines, bullet-focused"] F2["Required sections: Summary, Key Issues, Next Steps"] F3["outputs/pr_review.json — valid JSON with recommendation, summary, inlineComments, issueCounts"] F4["Each inline comment: path, line, startLine, side, comment, severity (BLOCKING|IMPORTANT|SUGGESTION)"] F5["comment must be a path to a file under outputs/pr_review_comments/.md"] F6["outputs/pr_review_general.md — max 1-2 paragraphs, factual, no essays"] F7["If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING (full logs in ci_failures_full.log)"] F8["Keep summary under 2 sentences — put details in inline comment files, not in general text"] F9["Severity classification follows general_guidelines.md:
BLOCKING = must fix · IMPORTANT = should fix · SUGGESTION = optional"] F10["Ticket context: verify PR changes satisfy ticket ACs — note gaps in review"] F11["Inline comments MUST target a line that appears in the PR diff
If the line is not in the diff, the comment becomes a general PR comment instead of a review thread"] F12["Use line numbers from the right-hand side of diff hunks
If pr_diff.txt is truncated, run git diff origin/{base}...HEAD to see the full diff"] ``` Example PR review outputs — keep concise: ### outputs/pr_review.json ```json { "recommendation": "BLOCK", "summary": "SQL injection in UserService.js must be fixed before merge.", "generalComment": "outputs/pr_review_general.md", "inlineComments": [ {"path":"src/auth/UserService.js","line":45,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","severity":"BLOCKING"}, {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":78,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","severity":"IMPORTANT"}, {"path":"src/utils/validation.js","line":23,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","severity":"SUGGESTION"} ], "issueCounts": {"blocking":1,"important":1,"suggestions":1} } ``` ### outputs/pr_review_general.md ```markdown ## Automated Code Review — BLOCK **Summary**: SQL injection blocks merge. One important issue (weak password validation) and one suggestion (extract duplicated validation). **Next Steps**: 1. Fix SQL injection in UserService.js — use parameterized queries 2. Strengthen password validation (8+ chars, mixed case, numbers, symbols) 3. Extract shared email validation utility ``` ### outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md ```markdown 🚨 **BLOCKING: SQL Injection** User input is interpolated directly into the query at `UserService.js:45`: ```javascript const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '${email}'`; ``` Use parameterized queries instead: ```javascript const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?'; await db.query(query, [email]); ``` ``` # Review verdict rules — machine protocol (binding) The review↔rework loop is a machine, not a conversation: your `recommendation` in `outputs/pr_review.json` is parsed mechanically and drives issue labels, rework runs and CI (each wasted round costs 15–20 CI minutes — gh-71). These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction (severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged. ## Verdict mapping Classify findings exactly as instructed: - 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss. - ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR works as shipped. - 💡 **SUGGESTION** — style, wording, import order, dartdoc refs, polish. Then map to the verdict: | Findings | `recommendation` | |---|---| | Any 🚨 BLOCKING (correctness/bug) | `REQUEST_CHANGES` — or `BLOCK` for security / data loss | | No 🚨 BLOCKING — only ⚠️ / 💡 remain | `APPROVE` | `APPROVE` with remaining ⚠️/💡 findings is the expected terminal state (`allowApproveWithSuggestions: true`): post every remaining finding as before (inline threads + general comment) — they do **not** block the merge and must **not** trigger another rework round. ## Anti-patterns (observed live, gh-71) - ❌ Returning `REQUEST_CHANGES` because a re-review surfaced new suggestion-level nits (docs wording, import style, dartdoc refs).
