## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

# 🚨 BLOCKING: `checkout_ref` is not a declared input of the leg workflow — GitHub 422s the fork dispatch with "Unexpected inputs provided", so the fix cannot fire in production

The rerouted fork dispatch now sends `inputs.checkout_ref` (`js/smAgent.js:756`, and a backfilled `inputs.pr` at :757 when the rule carries no `{prNumber}`), but the workflow it targets declares no such input. The dispatch target is the **target repo's** `ai-teammate.yml` — every deployment of it is a copy of this repo's `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`, whose `workflow_dispatch` block declares exactly four inputs: `issue`, `leg`, `reason`, `pr` (`workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template:45-67`). A repo-wide grep confirms `checkout_ref` exists nowhere in any workflow YAML — only in `smAgent.js` and the tests.

GitHub's dispatches REST endpoint validates the `inputs` object against the workflow file's declared inputs and rejects undeclared keys with 422 "Unexpected inputs provided" — documented live in [github/gh-aw#50027](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/50027) (`Failed to dispatch workflow "…": Unexpected inputs provided: ["ref"]` on `POST …/dispatches` — 422, fixed by stripping undeclared keys before sending).

The consequence chain makes AC1 worse than unmet:

1. The dispatch no longer 422s with "No ref found" (the rerouted ref is `main`, which exists) — it 422s with "Unexpected inputs provided: ["checkout_ref"]" **on every tick**.
2. `triggerFailures.classifyTriggerError` (`js/common/triggerFailures.js:56`) only maps "no ref found"-shaped messages to `'no-ref'`; this message classifies as `'transient'`.
3. So `recordDispatchFailure` returns at the `failClass !== 'no-ref'` gate — **no probe, no markers, no park, only a console warning**. A fork PR is still permanently undispatchable, but now with zero observability — strictly worse than the gh-922 state this card fixes.

The PR description defers "leg checkout/push **consumption** of the `checkout_ref` input" as out of scope — but *declaring* the input is not consumption; without a declaration the dispatch is rejected before any leg code runs, so IT-1 ("dispatch fires once") can never hold against the real GitHub endpoint. The IT-1 test passes only because `onTrigger` is mocked and never sees GitHub's input validation.

**Fix**: declare `checkout_ref` (and document `pr`) in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`'s `workflow_dispatch` inputs (consumption can stay in the #1074 lane), and add a workflow-lint/unit assertion so a future undeclared dispatch input fails CI instead of silently 422ing. Until then, `recommendation` stays REQUEST_CHANGES.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the gh-1028 single-writer leg guard is blind for rerouted fork dispatches — the run's `head_branch` is now `main`, not the fork branch

`headRefDispatch` preserves the guard's firing condition, but the guard's probe key — `it0.branch`, the fork branch name — no longer matches anything in the run list once the dispatch is rerouted. A `workflow_dispatch` run's `head_branch` is the dispatch ref (`main` after this PR), while `hasActiveLegRunOnBranch` still asks for runs whose `head_branch IS the dispatch branch` (`js/smAgent.js:678` → `:397` → `branchLegGuardModule.hasActiveLegRunOnBranch(runs, branch, …)`).

So for a fork PR the gh-1028 suppression can never see an in-flight leg: if both rework arms match the same fork PR (the issue-anchored rework-on-red-ci and the PR-anchored rework-on-label, exactly the gh-1028 live pathology on PR #1017), both dispatch, and two rework legs race the same fork head — with #1070 maintainer-edit pushes landing in the *fork*, the same double-push race gh-1028 was built to prevent. (Pre-gh-1075 this was latent because fork dispatches always 422'd; once the dispatch blocker is fixed this becomes live.)

Please key the probe on the pull ref (or `pr-<N>`) when `forkPlan.checkoutRef` is set — e.g. pass `forkPlan.checkoutRef || it0.branch` to `hasActiveLegRunOnBranch` — and add a regression test: fork PR + one in-flight leg run whose `head_branch` is `main` + a second dispatch arm → suppressed.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the pull-ref liveness probe is unauthenticated — on private base repos it always fails closed to "live" and AC3 parking silently never fires

`forkPullRefLive` probes `git ls-remote https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git refs/pull/<N>/head` with no credentials (`js/smAgent.js:848`). For a private base repo (the common case for machine targets) this errors with "Repository not found" on every probe; the catch then returns `true` (fail-open, per the gh-922 blind-tick invariant) — so a genuinely dead fork head on a private repo is **never** classified 'dead', never accumulates markers, never parks. AC3 ("genuinely dead fork heads still park") is silently void exactly where most of the fleet runs.

The rest of this codebase probes the *runner's authenticated remote* instead of a hardcoded public URL: `js/prepareTestPRForReview.js:214` (`git ls-remote --heads origin …`), `js/prepareCliTestReworkSetup.js:106`, `js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js:81` — the SM runs in a checkout of the base repo where `origin` already carries the token (cf. the `GH_TOKEN` push-URL handling at `js/smAgent.js:2037`).

**Fix**: probe `origin` (or a token-bearing URL assembled from split literals the way the existing push URLs are, so the token never appears contiguously in source): `git ls-remote origin refs/pull/<N>/head`. Keep the fail-open catch as-is. A unit test with a private-repo-shaped probe error (auth failure) asserting "never parks but logs a distinct degraded warning" would pin the intent.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the "fork deleted entirely" shape (`headRepo: null`) never reaches the pull-ref probe — the doc comment and the AC3 "keyed on the pull ref" claim don't hold for it

`forkDispatch.forkFullOf` fails closed to same-repo when `headRepo` is null, and the module comment (`js/common/forkDispatch.js:47-53`) names exactly that shape — "a deleted fork's REST payload carries head.repo:null" — as what "parks through the pull-ref probe". But with `headRepo` null the probe path here is **unreachable**:

1. `dispatchPlan` also sees `forkFullOf === null` → the plan is **not** rerouted → the dispatch still targets the fork branch → 422 "No ref found for: <fork-branch>".
2. Back in `recordDispatchFailure`, `forkFullOf(item, …)` is again null → the code drops to the same-repo branch (`js/smAgent.js:836`) → `expandedRef === item.branch` holds → `recordNoRefBookkeeping` keys the marker/park on the **branch name**, and no `ls-remote` probe ever runs.

So for the deleted-fork shape the AC3 outcome (a park) still happens — but through the pre-gh-1075 branch-keyed path, not "the existing no-ref path, keyed on the pull ref" as AC3 and the PR description state, and with no test coverage (every AC3 test keeps `headRepo: FORK_FULL` populated). Two consistency asks:

- Either route the null-`headRepo` + no-ref shape into the pull-ref probe (e.g. when `expandedRef === item.branch` and the branch is unfetchable on the base remote, treat as fork-suspect and probe `refs/pull/<N>/head`) — this also fixes a side effect: with the plan un-rerouted, a fork branch whose name collides with an existing base branch would dispatch on the *base* branch and validate the wrong code;
- or fix the comment/PR description/tests to state that the pull-ref-keyed park covers only the populated-`headRepo` case and the deleted-fork case parks branch-keyed via the legacy path.

Not blocking — parking still occurs — but the contract text and the tests currently describe a probe path the deleted-fork shape cannot reach.

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)

Now let me review the remaining rework difs: forkDispatch.js comments, test files. And check the new gate logic carefully:

**Concern A (title-keyed gate correctness)**: `hasActiveLegRunForPull` suppresses a fork dispatch when ANY active leg-workflow run carries the title token `· pr-<N>`. But the run title `▶ rework (SM) · pr-1591` is rendered for ANY PR-anchored dispatch (gh-544/#687 — PRs born without an issue also get `pr-<N>` titles), including **same-repo** PR-anchored legs dispatched on the branch. So if a same-repo PR-1591... wait, same-repo PR and fork PR can't share a number. Each PR number is unique per repo. So a run titled `pr-1591` belongs to PR 1591 regardless of fork/same-repo. The gate asks "is a leg already in flight for THIS PR" — a same-repo leg for PR 1591 would suppress a fork dispatch for PR 1591 — but that can't happen since a PR is either same-repo or fork. OK.

But subtle: what about a COMPLETED-but-fresh run? Active statuses only (queued/in_progress/waiting/pending). OK.

Another subtlety: the gate keys on title token `pr-1591` — but the branch-keyed gate ALSO fires fork dispatches? No — fork, only the pull gate fires. What if a fork PR's leg was dispatched by an OLD SM version on the branch (pre-reroute, e.g. mixed-version fleet)? head_branch = fork branch; pull gate checks `matchesBranch(run, pullHeadRefOf(prNumber))` — fork branch ≠ pull ref; title may carry pr-1591 if inputs.pr set. If the old dispatch didn't backfill pr... then the in-flight run is invisible to the new gate. Transitional edge, negligible.

**Concern B**: `legRunOwnsPull` checks `isLegRun(run, workflowFile)` — same vocabulary as branch gate. OK.

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine logins ride the
      # deployment-level input (#687, gh-728), exactly like the factory's
      # contract. Comma-separated LIST: the agent harness bot AND the CI
      # bot — github-actions[bot] authors its own PRs (live fa PR #1249)
      # and must ride the machine path (owner directive 2026-10-05).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # App auth (awf#52): minted installation token wins over the PAT
      # inside the factory when both secrets are present.
      APP_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

## PR Description

Closes #1075
### What changed
Cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: a head-targeted dispatch for a fork PR reroutes onto the base repo's standard machine ref (`main`) with the PR number and a `refs/pull/<N>/head` checkout plan in the run inputs, instead of dispatching on the fork branch which 422s forever in the base repo (live fa pr-1591). The no-ref bookkeeping now keys fork heads to the `refs/pull/<N>/head` liveness probe instead of the branch name.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/forkDispatch.js`: `dispatchPlan` (fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PRs unchanged), `classifyForkNoRef`, `forkFullOf` (reuses the gh-1070 `validationLiveness.forkHeadFull` case-insensitive same-repo compare — no second resolver).
- `triggerWorkflow` applies the plan before dispatch and backfills `inputs.pr` only when the rule carried no `{prNumber}`; the gh-1028 branch-leg guard keeps its pre-gh-1075 semantics via a captured `headRefDispatch` flag.
- `recordDispatchFailure`: a no-ref failure on a fork PR runs an `ls-remote refs/pull/<N>/head` probe (fail-open to LIVE) — fetchable → never head-dead, no markers/park (AC2); unfetchable → parks through the existing gh-922 path keyed on the pull ref (AC3). Same-repo bookkeeping is byte-identical (REG-1); the gh-1028/715/1029 guards and the leg push-back (#1070 contract) are untouched.
- Leg checkout/push consumption of the `checkout_ref` input is deliberately out of scope (card non-goals; #1074 owns failure observability).

The dispatch target is the **target repo's** `ai-teammate.yml` — every deployment of it is a copy of this repo's `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`, whose `workflow_dispatch` block declares exactly four inputs: `issue`, `leg`, `reason`, `pr` (`workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template:45-67`). GitHub's dispatches REST endpoint validates the `inputs` object against the workflow file's declared inputs and rejects undeclared keys with 422 "Unexpected inputs provided" — documented live in [github/gh-aw#50027](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/50027) (`Failed to dispatch workflow "…": Unexpected inputs provided: ["ref"]` on `POST …/dispatches` — 422, fixed by stripping undeclared keys before sending).

1. The dispatch no longer 422s with "No ref found" (the rerouted ref is `main`, which exists) — it 422s with "Unexpected inputs provided: ["checkout_ref"]" **on every tick**.
2. `triggerFailures.classifyTriggerError` (`js/common/triggerFailures.js:56`) only maps "no ref found"-shaped messages to `'no-ref'`; this message classifies as `'transient'`.
3. So `recordDispatchFailure` returns at the `failClass !== 'no-ref'` gate — **no probe, no markers, no park, only a console warning**. A fork PR is still permanently undispatchable, but now with zero observability — strictly worse than the gh-922 state this card fixes.

The PR description defers "leg checkout/push **consumption** of the `checkout_ref` input" as out of scope — but *declaring* the input is not consumption; without a declaration the dispatch is rejected before any leg code runs, so IT-1 ("dispatch fires once") can never hold against the real GitHub endpoint. The IT-1 test passes only because `onTrigger` is mocked and never sees GitHub's input validation.

**Fix**: declare `checkout_ref` (and document `pr`) in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`'s `workflow_dispatch` inputs (consumption can stay in the #1074 lane), and add a workflow-lint/unit assertion so a future undeclared dispatch input fails CI instead of silently 422ing. blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)

The CRAP check measures per-function CRAP with a threshold of 8 for new/renamed functions. The rework added 459 lines including complexity to `smAgent.js` (recordDispatchFailure, forkPullRefLive, triggerWorkflow, hasActiveLegRunForPull) — the likely CRAP regression. `recordDispatchFailure` was already flagged in the codebase as high-CRAP territory (the gh-925 comment "worst in the repo" was about scm provider).

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine logins ride the
      # deployment-level input (#687, gh-728), exactly like the factory's
      # contract. Comma-separated LIST: the agent harness bot AND the CI
      # bot — github-actions[bot] authors its own PRs (live fa PR #1249)
      # and must ride the machine path (owner directive 2026-10-05).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # App auth (awf#52): minted installation token wins over the PAT
      # inside the factory when both secrets are present.
      APP_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]

- **Updated**: 2026-10-19T07:58:52Z

## PR Description

Closes #1075
### What changed
Cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: a head-targeted dispatch for a fork PR reroutes onto the base repo's standard machine ref (`main`) with the PR number and a `refs/pull/<N>/head` checkout plan in the run inputs, instead of dispatching on the fork branch which 422s forever in the base repo (live fa pr-1591). The no-ref bookkeeping now keys fork heads to the `refs/pull/<N>/head` liveness probe instead of the branch name.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/forkDispatch.js`: `dispatchPlan` (fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PRs unchanged), `classifyForkNoRef`, `forkFullOf` (reuses the gh-1070 `validationLiveness.forkHeadFull` case-insensitive same-repo compare — no second resolver).
- `triggerWorkflow` applies the plan before dispatch and backfills `inputs.pr` only when the rule carried no `{prNumber}`; the gh-1028 branch-leg guard keeps its pre-gh-1075 semantics via a captured `headRefDispatch` flag.
- `recordDispatchFailure`: a no-ref failure on a fork PR runs an `ls-remote refs/pull/<N>/head` probe (fail-open to LIVE) — fetchable → never head-dead, no markers/park (AC2); unfetchable → parks through the existing gh-922 path keyed on the pull ref (AC3). Same-repo bookkeeping is byte-identical (REG-1); the gh-1028/715/1029 guards and the leg push-back (#1070 contract) are untouched.
- Leg checkout/push consumption of the `checkout_ref` input is deliberately out of scope (card non-goals; #1074 owns failure observability).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_forkDispatch.json   # UT-1/UT-2 pure contract (12 tests)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json        # IT-1/AC2/AC3/REG-1 tick suites (623 tests)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite — 4594 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Dispatch flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SM[SM tick: fork PR candidate] --> PLAN[forkDispatch.dispatchPlan]
  PLAN -->|same-repo| BR[ref: branch — unchanged]
  PLAN -->|cross-repo| MAIN[ref: main + inputs.checkout_ref = refs/pull/N/head]
  MAIN --> LEG[leg runs base workflow, checks out refs/pull/N/head]
  MAIN -. 422 no-ref .-> PROBE[ls-remote refs/pull/N/head]
  PROBE -->|fetchable| OK[not head-dead — no markers, no park]
  PROBE -->|unfetchable| PARK[gh-922 park keyed on the pull ref]
```

</details>

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

# 🚨 BLOCKING: `checkout_ref` is not a declared input of the leg workflow — GitHub 422s the fork dispatch with "Unexpected inputs provided", so the fix cannot fire in production

The rerouted fork dispatch now sends `inputs.checkout_ref` (`js/smAgent.js:756`, and a backfilled `inputs.pr` at :757 when the rule carries no `{prNumber}`), but the workflow it targets declares no such input. The dispatch target is the **target repo's** `ai-teammate.yml` — every deployment of it is a copy of this repo's `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`, whose `workflow_dispatch` block declares exactly four inputs: `issue`, `leg`, `reason`, `pr` (`workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template:45-67`). A repo-wide grep confirms `checkout_ref` exists nowhere in any workflow YAML — only in `smAgent.js` and the tests.

GitHub's dispatches REST endpoint validates the `inputs` object against the workflow file's declared inputs and rejects undeclared keys with 422 "Unexpected inputs provided" — documented live in [github/gh-aw#50027](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/50027) (`Failed to dispatch workflow "…": Unexpected inputs provided: ["ref"]` on `POST …/dispatches` — 422, fixed by stripping undeclared keys before sending).

The consequence chain makes AC1 worse than unmet:

1. The dispatch no longer 422s with "No ref found" (the rerouted ref is `main`, which exists) — it 422s with "Unexpected inputs provided: ["checkout_ref"]" **on every tick**.
2. `triggerFailures.classifyTriggerError` (`js/common/triggerFailures.js:56`) only maps "no ref found"-shaped messages to `'no-ref'`; this message classifies as `'transient'`.
3. So `recordDispatchFailure` returns at the `failClass !== 'no-ref'` gate — **no probe, no markers, no park, only a console warning**. A fork PR is still permanently undispatchable, but now with zero observability — strictly worse than the gh-922 state this card fixes.

The PR description defers "leg checkout/push **consumption** of the `checkout_ref` input" as out of scope — but *declaring* the input is not consumption; without a declaration the dispatch is rejected before any leg code runs, so IT-1 ("dispatch fires once") can never hold against the real GitHub endpoint. The IT-1 test passes only because `onTrigger` is mocked and never sees GitHub's input validation.

**Fix**: declare `checkout_ref` (and document `pr`) in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`'s `workflow_dispatch` inputs (consumption can stay in the #1074 lane), and add a workflow-lint/unit assertion so a future undeclared dispatch input fails CI instead of silently 422ing. Until then, `recommendation` stays REQUEST_CHANGES.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the gh-1028 single-writer leg guard is blind for rerouted fork dispatches — the run's `head_branch` is now `main`, not the fork branch

`headRefDispatch` preserves the guard's firing condition, but the guard's probe key — `it0.branch`, the fork branch name — no longer matches anything in the run list once the dispatch is rerouted. A `workflow_dispatch` run's `head_branch` is the dispatch ref (`main` after this PR), while `hasActiveLegRunOnBranch` still asks for runs whose `head_branch IS the dispatch branch` (`js/smAgent.js:678` → `:397` → `branchLegGuardModule.hasActiveLegRunOnBranch(runs, branch, …)`).

So for a fork PR the gh-1028 suppression can never see an in-flight leg: if both rework arms match the same fork PR (the issue-anchored rework-on-red-ci and the PR-anchored rework-on-label, exactly the gh-1028 live pathology on PR #1017), both dispatch, and two rework legs race the same fork head — with #1070 maintainer-edit pushes landing in the *fork*, the same double-push race gh-1028 was built to prevent. (Pre-gh-1075 this was latent because fork dispatches always 422'd; once the dispatch blocker is fixed this becomes live.)

Please key the probe on the pull ref (or `pr-<N>`) when `forkPlan.checkoutRef` is set — e.g. pass `forkPlan.checkoutRef || it0.branch` to `hasActiveLegRunOnBranch` — and add a regression test: fork PR + one in-flight leg run whose `head_branch` is `main` + a second dispatch arm → suppressed.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the pull-ref liveness probe is unauthenticated — on private base repos it always fails closed to "live" and AC3 parking silently never fires

`forkPullRefLive` probes `git ls-remote https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git refs/pull/<N>/head` with no credentials (`js/smAgent.js:848`). For a private base repo (the common case for machine targets) this errors with "Repository not found" on every probe; the catch then returns `true` (fail-open, per the gh-922 blind-tick invariant) — so a genuinely dead fork head on a private repo is **never** classified 'dead', never accumulates markers, never parks. AC3 ("genuinely dead fork heads still park") is silently void exactly where most of the fleet runs.

The rest of this codebase probes the *runner's authenticated remote* instead of a hardcoded public URL: `js/prepareTestPRForReview.js:214` (`git ls-remote --heads origin …`), `js/prepareCliTestReworkSetup.js:106`, `js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js:81` — the SM runs in a checkout of the base repo where `origin` already carries the token (cf. the `GH_TOKEN` push-URL handling at `js/smAgent.js:2037`).

**Fix**: probe `origin` (or a token-bearing URL assembled from split literals the way the existing push URLs are, so the token never appears contiguously in source): `git ls-remote origin refs/pull/<N>/head`. Keep the fail-open catch as-is. A unit test with a private-repo-shaped probe error (auth failure) asserting "never parks but logs a distinct degraded warning" would pin the intent.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the "fork deleted entirely" shape (`headRepo: null`) never reaches the pull-ref probe — the doc comment and the AC3 "keyed on the pull ref" claim don't hold for it

`forkDispatch.forkFullOf` fails closed to same-repo when `headRepo` is null, and the module comment (`js/common/forkDispatch.js:47-53`) names exactly that shape — "a deleted fork's REST payload carries head.repo:null" — as what "parks through the pull-ref probe". But with `headRepo` null the probe path here is **unreachable**:

1. `dispatchPlan` also sees `forkFullOf === null` → the plan is **not** rerouted → the dispatch still targets the fork branch → 422 "No ref found for: <fork-branch>".
2. Back in `recordDispatchFailure`, `forkFullOf(item, …)` is again null → the code drops to the same-repo branch (`js/smAgent.js:836`) → `expandedRef === item.branch` holds → `recordNoRefBookkeeping` keys the marker/park on the **branch name**, and no `ls-remote` probe ever runs.

So for the deleted-fork shape the AC3 outcome (a park) still happens — but through the pre-gh-1075 branch-keyed path, not "the existing no-ref path, keyed on the pull ref" as AC3 and the PR description state, and with no test coverage (every AC3 test keeps `headRepo: FORK_FULL` populated). Two consistency asks:

- Either route the null-`headRepo` + no-ref shape into the pull-ref probe (e.g. when `expandedRef === item.branch` and the branch is unfetchable on the base remote, treat as fork-suspect and probe `refs/pull/<N>/head`) — this also fixes a side effect: with the plan un-rerouted, a fork branch whose name collides with an existing base branch would dispatch on the *base* branch and validate the wrong code;
- or fix the comment/PR description/tests to state that the pull-ref-keyed park covers only the populated-`headRepo` case and the deleted-fork case parks branch-keyed via the legacy path.

Not blocking — parking still occurs — but the contract text and the tests currently describe a probe path the deleted-fork shape cannot reach.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository …

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine logins ride the
      # deployment-level input (#687, gh-728), exactly like the factory's
      # contract. Comma-separated LIST: the agent harness bot AND the CI
      # bot — github-actions[bot] authors its own PRs (live fa PR #1249)
      # and must ride the machine path (owner directive 2026-10-05).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # App auth (awf#52): minted installation token wins over the PAT
      # inside the factory when both secrets are present.
      APP_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

# 🚨 BLOCKING: the `crap` CI check fails on this head — 3 new functions over `CRAP_THRESHOLD=8`

The quality gate on head `a2013520` (run 39218810451) fails the CRAP ratchet:

```
CRAP ratchet failed: CRAP may only decrease.
NEW > 8  js/common/branchLegGuard.js::titleHasPrToken: 16
NEW > 8  js/common/branchLegGuard.js::legRunOwnsPull: 8.1
NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_forkDispatch.js::declaredDispatchInputs: 10
0 regression(s), 3 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

All three are introduced by this PR, and `CRAP_THRESHOLD=8` applies to functions not in the released baseline (`.github/workflows/quality.yml:53`) — so they block merge until the complexity drops or the coverage of their branches rises.

Suggested splits:

- `titleHasPrToken` (js/common/branchLegGuard.js:167): the CRAP driver is the inline boundary-char logic inside the `while` loop. Extract two named predicates — e.g. `isDigitOrDash(ch)` and `isWordChar(ch)` (mirroring `smAgent.isAnchorKeyChar`, js/smAgent.js:307) — or precompute the boundary test once per index. That cuts the cyclomatic load per loop iteration roughly in half; the existing 8 pure tests in `test_branchLegGuard.js` then cover the branches.
- `legRunOwnsPull` (js/common/branchLegGuard.js:191, 8.1 — marginally over): folding the two `isActiveStatus`/staleness guards into the existing shared vocabulary helpers (or a one-line `isFreshActiveRun(run, nowMs, staleMs)`) should bring it under 8.
- `declaredDispatchInputs` (js/unit-tests/test_forkDispatch.js:129, 10): the indentation state machine carries the whole cost. Extracting the `inputs:`-block slicer (find the `inputs:` line by indentation, collect deeper-indented keys until dedent) as a small helper drops the loop's branching; the two lint tests already exercise both outcomes.

Not style-polish — a red required gate; merge is blocked until the ratchet is green.

# 🚨 BLOCKING: `git ls-remote origin` probes the ENGINE checkout, not the target repo — on any SM whose target ≠ engine repo, live fork PRs are misclassified 'dead' and wrongly parked

This reworks the probe onto `origin`, but in the SM's runtime `origin` is the **engine** repo, not the repo named by `repoInfo`. The codebase documents this itself at `js/smAgent.js:2049-2051` (the gh-1070 silent-update comment, live-verified): *"The reconcile job's working directory is the dmtools-agents engine checkout (live: `git fetch origin` there fetched dmtools-agents and every PR pathspec 404'd) — the builder clones the TARGET repo instead."* That is exactly why `silentUpdateCommand` does `gh repo clone <owner>/<repo> <dir>` instead of touching `origin`. My round-1 suggestion to "probe `origin`" was written for a legs-style runtime (which runs inside a target checkout, like `prepareTestPRForReview.js:214`) — for the SM dispatch loop it is the wrong remote, and I should have caught that context difference then.

Consequence for every SM managing a repo other than the engine checkout (the dynamic-repo fleet — the gh-1075 test fixture's own world is `epam/dmtools-dart` managed from the dmtools-agents engine):

1. Engine repo has no `refs/pull/<N>/head` → empty output → `'dead'` → a **live** fork head in the TARGET repo accumulates `trigger-failed refs/pull/<N>/head` markers and gets parked `validation_failed` at the cap. AC2 inverted with real damage: wrong markers and a wrong park on a healthy PR.
2. Engine repo happens to have a PR `#N` → fetchable → `'live'` — the right verdict reached about the wrong repository, by luck.

(The fa self-host works only because target == engine makes `origin` coincidentally correct — the live incident's repo, but not the fleet.)

**Fix**: probe the target repo named by the now-unused `repoInfo` parameter, authenticated, with the established split-literal token URL idiom (`validationLiveness.forkPushTokenUrl`, js/common/validationLiveness.js — `'https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/' + owner + '/' + repo + '.git'`; `${GH_TOKEN}` interpolates in the child env exactly like the existing silent-update commands, so the secret never appears in source or the captured command string):

```javascript
command: 'git ls-remote ' +
    "'https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/'" + ' + ' // split-literal idiom
    ...
```

or the equivalent. Keep the DEGRADED fail-open catch. Then the `origin` test (and its `https://github.com/` negative assertion) flips to assert the command names `<owner>/<repo>` from `repoInfo`.

## PR Description

Closes #1075
### What changed
Cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: a head-targeted dispatch for a fork PR reroutes onto the base repo's standard machine ref (`main`) with the PR number and a `refs/pull/<N>/head` checkout plan in the run inputs, instead of dispatching on the fork branch which 422s forever in the base repo (live fa pr-1591). The no-ref bookkeeping now keys fork heads to the `refs/pull/<N>/head` liveness probe instead of the branch name.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/forkDispatch.js`: `dispatchPlan` (fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PRs unchanged), `classifyForkNoRef`, `forkFullOf` (reuses the gh-1070 `validationLiveness.forkHeadFull` case-insensitive same-repo compare — no second resolver).
- `triggerWorkflow` applies the plan before dispatch and backfills `inputs.pr` only when the rule carried no `{prNumber}`; the gh-1028 branch-leg guard keeps its pre-gh-1075 semantics via a captured `headRefDispatch` flag.
- `recordDispatchFailure`: a no-ref failure on a fork PR runs an `ls-remote refs/pull/<N>/head` probe (fail-open to LIVE) — fetchable → never head-dead, no markers/park (AC2); unfetchable → parks through the existing gh-922 path keyed on the pull ref (AC3). Same-repo bookkeeping is byte-identical (REG-1); the gh-1028/715/1029 guards and the leg push-back (#1070 contract) are untouched.
- Leg checkout/push consumption of the `checkout_ref` input is deliberately out of scope (card non-goals; #1074 owns failure observability).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_forkDispatch.json   # UT-1/UT-2 pure contract (12 tests)
```

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

# 🚨 BLOCKING: `checkout_ref` is not a declared input of the leg workflow — GitHub 422s the fork dispatch with "Unexpected inputs provided", so the fix cannot fire in production

The rerouted fork dispatch now sends `inputs.checkout_ref` (`js/smAgent.js:756`, and a backfilled `inputs.pr` at :757 when the rule carries no `{prNumber}`), but the workflow it targets declares no such input. The dispatch target is the **target repo's** `ai-teammate.yml` — every deployment of it is a copy of this repo's `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`, whose `workflow_dispatch` block declares exactly four inputs: `issue`, `leg`, `reason`, `pr` (`workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template:45-67`). A repo-wide grep confirms `checkout_ref` exists nowhere in any workflow YAML — only in `smAgent.js` and the tests.

GitHub's dispatches REST endpoint validates the `inputs` object against the workflow file's declared inputs and rejects undeclared keys with 422 "Unexpected inputs provided" — documented live in [github/gh-aw#50027](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/50027) (`Failed to dispatch workflow "…": Unexpected inputs provided: ["ref"]` on `POST …/dispatches` — 422, fixed by stripping undeclared keys before sending).

The consequence chain makes AC1 worse than unmet:

1. The dispatch no longer 422s with "No ref found" (the rerouted ref is `main`, which exists) — it 422s with "Unexpected inputs provided: ["checkout_ref"]" **on every tick**.
2. `triggerFailures.classifyTriggerError` (`js/common/triggerFailures.js:56`) only maps "no ref found"-shaped messages to `'no-ref'`; this message classifies as `'transient'`.
3. So `recordDispatchFailure` returns at the `failClass !== 'no-ref'` gate — **no probe, no markers, no park, only a console warning**. A fork PR is still permanently undispatchable, but now with zero observability — strictly worse than the gh-922 state this card fixes.

The PR description defers "leg checkout/push **consumption** of the `checkout_ref` input" as out of scope — but *declaring* the input is not consumption; without a declaration the dispatch is rejected before any leg code runs, so IT-1 ("dispatch fires once") can never hold against the real GitHub endpoint. The IT-1 test passes only because `onTrigger` is mocked and never sees GitHub's input validation.

**Fix**: declare `checkout_ref` (and document `pr`) in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`'s `workflow_dispatch` inputs (consumption can stay in the #1074 lane), and add a workflow-lint/unit assertion so a future undeclared dispatch input fails CI instead of silently 422ing. Until then, `recommendation` stays REQUEST_CHANGES.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the gh-1028 single-writer leg guard is blind for rerouted fork dispatches — the run's `head_branch` is now `main`, not the fork branch

`headRefDispatch` preserves the guard's firing condition, but the guard's probe key — `it0.branch`, the fork branch name — no longer matches anything in the run list once the dispatch is rerouted. A `workflow_dispatch` run's `head_branch` is the dispatch ref (`main` after this PR), while `hasActiveLegRunOnBranch` still asks for runs whose `head_branch IS the dispatch branch` (`js/smAgent.js:678` → `:397` → `branchLegGuardModule.hasActiveLegRunOnBranch(runs, branch, …)`).

So for a fork PR the gh-1028 suppression can never see an in-flight leg: if both rework arms match the same fork PR (the issue-anchored rework-on-red-ci and the PR-anchored rework-on-label, exactly the gh-1028 live pathology on PR #1017), both dispatch, and two rework legs race the same fork head — with #1070 maintainer-edit pushes landing in the *fork*, the same double-push race gh-1028 was built to prevent. (Pre-gh-1075 this was latent because fork dispatches always 422'd; once the dispatch blocker is fixed this becomes live.)

Please key the probe on the pull ref (or `pr-<N>`) when `forkPlan.checkoutRef` is set — e.g. pass `forkPlan.checkoutRef || it0.branch` to `hasActiveLegRunOnBranch` — and add a regression test: fork PR + one in-flight leg run whose `head_branch` is `main` + a second dispatch arm → suppressed.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the pull-ref liveness probe is unauthenticated — on private base repos it always fails closed to "live" and AC3 parking silently never fires

`forkPullRefLive` probes `git ls-remote https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git refs/pull/<N>/head` with no credentials (`js/smAgent.js:848`). For a private base repo (the common case for machine targets) this errors with "Repository not found" on every probe; the catch then returns `true` (fail-open, per the gh-922 blind-tick invariant) — so a genuinely dead fork head on a private repo is **never** classified 'dead', never accumulates markers, never parks. AC3 ("genuinely dead fork heads still park") is silently void exactly where most of the fleet runs.

The rest of this codebase probes the *runner's authenticated remote* instead of a hardcoded public URL: `js/prepareTestPRForReview.js:214` (`git ls-remote --heads origin …`), `js/prepareCliTestReworkSetup.js:106`, `js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js:81` — the SM runs in a checkout of the base repo where `origin` already carries the token (cf. the `GH_TOKEN` push-URL handling at `js/smAgent.js:2037`).

**Fix**: probe `origin` (or a token-bearing URL assembled from split literals the way the existing push URLs are, so the token never appears contiguously in source): `git ls-remote origin refs/pull/<N>/head`. Keep the fail-open catch as-is. A unit test with a private-repo-shaped probe error (auth failure) asserting "never parks but logs a distinct degraded warning" would pin the intent.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-19):

# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the "fork deleted entirely" shape (`headRepo: null`) never reaches the pull-ref probe — the doc comment and the AC3 "keyed on the pull ref" claim don't hold for it

`forkDispatch.forkFullOf` fails closed to same-repo when `headRepo` is null, and the module comment (`js/common/forkDispatch.js:47-53`) names exactly that shape — "a deleted fork's REST payload carries head.repo:null" — as what "parks through the pull-ref probe". But with `headRepo` null the probe path here is **unreachable**:

1. `dispatchPlan` also sees `forkFullOf === null` → the plan is **not** rerouted → the dispatch still targets the fork branch → 422 "No ref found for: <fork-branch>".
2. Back in `recordDispatchFailure`, `forkFullOf(item, …)` is again null → the code drops to the same-repo branch (`js/smAgent.js:836`) → `expandedRef === item.branch` holds → `recordNoRefBookkeeping` keys the marker/park on the **branch name**, and no `ls-remote` probe ever runs.

So for the deleted-fork shape the AC3 outcome (a park) still happens — but through the pre-gh-1075 branch-keyed path, not "the existing no-ref path, keyed on the pull ref" as AC3 and the PR description state, and with no test coverage (every AC3 test keeps `headRepo: FORK_FULL` populated). Two consistency asks:

- Either route the null-`headRepo` + no-ref shape into the pull-ref probe (e.g. when `expandedRef === item.branch` and the branch is unfetchable on the base remote, treat as fork-suspect and probe `refs/pull/<N>/head`) — this also fixes a side effect: with the plan un-rerouted, a fork branch whose name collides with an existing base branch would dispatch on the *base* branch and validate the wrong code;
- or fix the comment/PR description/tests to state that the pull-ref-keyed park covers only the populated-`headRepo` case and the deleted-fork case parks branch-keyed via the legacy path.

Not blocking — parking still occurs — but the contract text and the tests currently describe a probe path the deleted-fork shape cannot reach.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine logins ride the
      # deployment-level input (#687, gh-728), exactly like the factory's
      # contract. Comma-separated LIST: the agent harness bot AND the CI
      # bot — github-actions[bot] authors its own PRs (live fa PR #1249)
      # and must ride the machine path (owner directive 2026-10-05).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # App auth (awf#52): minted installation token wins over the PAT
      # inside the factory when both secrets are present.
      APP_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the new gh-1028 fork gate keys on the run-title `pr-<N>` anchor — but the self-host leg stub's `run-name` never renders `pr-<N>`, so the gate is blind exactly on the live-incident repo

The gate's whole premise (documented here, in `branchLegGuard.js` and in the test) is: *"the leg workflow's run-name renders '▶ <leg> (SM) · pr-<N>' whenever inputs.pr is set"* — that is the **template's** run-name (`workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template:31-41`). But the self-host stub this repo actually dispatches (`.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml:32`) has a different run-name under the gh-1065 contract:

```
teammate: <event> #<issue.number || inputs.issue> <leg || label-derived>
```

It echoes `inputs.issue`, never `inputs.pr` — a PR-anchored fork leg in the dmtools-agents repo (the live pr-1591 incident's home) runs as `teammate: workflow_dispatch #  rework` with `head_branch: main`. `titleHasPrToken` finds no `pr-1591` token, the `head_branch === refs/pull/1591/head` forward-compat doesn't apply, and `hasActiveLegRunForPull` matches nothing → the gh-1028 suppression silently degrades to "never suppress" for self-host fork PRs (the titless-run test even pins this degrade as fail-open). Both rework arms matching the same fork PR can double-dispatch and race their fork pushes — the gh-1028 pathology the rework set out to close.

**Fix**: add the `pr-<N>` token to the stub's run-name under the existing gh-1065 leg-title contract (e.g. append `${ inputs.pr != '' && format('· pr-{0}', inputs.pr) }`, preserving the trailing-leg token `legOfRunName` parses), or give `legRunOwnsPull` a fallback discriminator for workflows whose run-name predates the anchor. A unit test pinning the stub's run-name shape (the way `test_workflowLint.js` guards trigger/dedup invariants) would keep the two run-name dialects from drifting again.

## Review complete — `REQUEST_CHANGES` (1 BLOCKING, 4 IMPORTANT, 1 SUGGESTION)

**🚨 Blocker — the fix cannot fire in production.** The rerouted fork dispatch sends `inputs.checkout_ref` (`js/smAgent.js:756`), but the leg workflow it targets declares no such input — `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template:45-67` declares only `issue`/`leg`/`reason`/`pr`, and repo-wide grep shows `checkout_ref` in no workflow YAML. GitHub's dispatches endpoint rejects undeclared inputs with 422 "Unexpected inputs provided" (cited: [github/gh-aw#50027](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/issues/50027), read this run), and `classifyTriggerError` maps that to `transient` → no probe, no markers, no park. Fork PRs stay permanently undispatchable — now silently. Declaring the input is not the deferred "consumption" work; without it the dispatch is rejected before any leg runs.

**⚠️ Important findings:**
- `js/smAgent.js:678` — the gh-1028 single-writer leg guard probes the fork branch name, but rerouted runs have `head_branch = main` → guard never matches; two rework arms can double-dispatch on a fork head (the PR #1017 race, now with fork pushes).
- `js/smAgent.js:848` — the `ls-remote` probe uses an unauthenticated public HTTPS URL; on private base repos it always fails closed-to-live, silently voiding AC3 parking. Codebase convention (`origin`, authenticated) exists at `prepareTestPRForReview.js:214` etc.
- `js/smAgent.js:820` — the deleted-fork shape (`headRepo:null`, named in the module's own comment) never reaches the pull-ref probe: no reroute in `dispatchPlan` either, so it 422s on the branch and parks *branch-keyed* via the legacy path — contradicting AC3/"keyed on the pull ref" and untested.
- `js/smAgent.js:825` — the shared `recordDispatchFailure` also serves the un-rerouted `validate_pr` CI lane (`:3411`), whose structural fork 422s are now fully silenced; validation can never arm for fork PRs with zero trace.

**💡 Suggestion:** park-comment wording for fork parks ("re-push the branch" when the fork is gone).

## PR Description

Closes #1075
### What changed
Cross-repo (fork) PRs are dispatchable: a head-targeted dispatch for a fork PR reroutes onto the base repo's standard machine ref (`main`) with the PR number and a `refs/pull/<N>/head` checkout plan in the run inputs, instead of dispatching on the fork branch which 422s forever in the base repo (live fa pr-1591). The no-ref bookkeeping now keys fork heads to the `refs/pull/<N>/head` liveness probe instead of the branch name.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/forkDispatch.js`: `dispatchPlan` (fork PR → base ref + pull-ref checkout plan; same-repo PRs unchanged), `classifyForkNoRef`, `forkFullOf` (reuses the gh-1070 `validationLiveness.forkHeadFull` case-insensitive same-repo compare — no second resolver).
- `triggerWorkflow` applies the plan before dispatch and backfills `inputs.pr` only when the rule carried no `{prNumber}`; the gh-1028 branch-leg guard keeps its pre-gh-1075 semantics via a captured `headRefDispatch` flag.
- `recordDispatchFailure`: a no-ref failure on a fork PR runs an `ls-remote refs/pull/<N>/head` probe (fail-open to LIVE) — fetchable → never head-dead, no markers/park (AC2); unfetchable → parks through the existing gh-922 path keyed on the pull ref (AC3). Same-repo bookkeeping is byte-identical (REG-1); the gh-1028/715/1029 guards and the leg push-back (#1070 contract) are untouched.
- Leg checkout/push consumption of the `checkout_ref` input is deliberately out of scope (card non-goals; #1074 owns failure observability).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_forkDispatch.json   # UT-1/UT-2 pure contract (12 tests)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json        # IT-1/AC2/AC3/REG-1 tick suites (623 tests)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite — 4594 passed, 0 failed
```

```mermaid
  PLAN -->|same-repo| BR[ref: branch — unchanged]

  MAIN --> LEG[leg runs base workflow, checks out refs/pull/N/head]
```
